If various APIs or intermediates are manufactured in the same equipment and the equipment is cleaned by the same process, a representative intermediate or API can be selected for cleaning validation. This selection should be based on the solubility and difficulty of cleaning and the calculation of residue limits based on potency, toxicity, and stability.
ref_texts.EU GMP Part II 12.72: 12.72 The cleaning validation protocol should describe the equipment to be cleaned, procedures, materials, acceptable cleaning levels, parameters to be monitored and controlled, and analytical methods. The protocol should also indicate the type of samples to be obtained and how they are collected and labelled.
ref_texts.EU GMP Part II 12.74: 12.74 Validated analytical methods having sensitivity to detect residues or contaminants should be used. The detection limit for each analytical method should be sufficiently sensitive to detect the established acceptable level of the residue or contaminant. The method’s attainable recovery level should be established. Residue limits should be practical, achievable, verifiable and based on the most deleterious residue. Limits can be established based on the minimum known pharmacological, toxicological, or physiological activity of the API or its most deleterious component.
ref_texts.EU GMP Part II 12.80: 12.80 Analytical methods should be validated unless the method employed is included in the relevant pharmacopoeia or other recognised standard reference. The suitability of all testing methods used should nonetheless be verified under actual conditions of use and documented.
ref_texts.EU GMP Part II 12.81: 12.81 Methods should be validated to include consideration of characteristics included within the ICH guidelines on validation of analytical methods. The degree of analytical validation performed should reflect the purpose of the analysis and the stage of the API production process.
ref_texts.EU GMP Part II 12.82: 12.82 Appropriate qualification of analytical equipment should be considered before starting validation of analytical methods.
ref_texts.EU GMP Part II 12.83: 12.83 Complete records should be maintained of any modification of a validated analytical method. Such records should include the reason for the modification and appropriate data to verify that the modification produces results that are as accurate and reliable as the established method.
ref_texts.EU GMP Part II 19.60: 19.60 Process validation for the production of APIs for use in clinical trials is normally inappropriate, where a single API batch is produced or where process changes during API development make batch replication difficult or inexact. The combination of controls, calibration, and, where appropriate, equipment qualification assures API quality during this development phase.
ref_texts.EU GMP Part II 5.40: 5.40 GMP related computerized systems should be validated. The depth and scope of validation depends on the diversity, complexity and criticality of the computerized application.
ref_texts.EU GMP Part II 5.41: 5.41 Appropriate installation qualification and operational qualification should demonstrate the suitability of computer hardware and software to perform assigned tasks.
ref_texts.EU GMP Part II 5.42: 5.42 Commercially available software that has been qualified does not require the same level of testing. If an existing system was not validated at time of installation, a retrospective validation could be conducted if appropriate documentation is available.
ref_texts.EU GMP Part II 5.43: 5.43 Computerized systems should have sufficient controls to prevent unauthorized access or changes to data. There should be controls to prevent omissions in data (e.g. system turned off and data not captured). There should be a record of any data change made, the previous entry, who made the change, and when the change was made.
ref_texts.EU GMP Part II 5.44: 5.44 Written procedures should be available for the operation and maintenance of computerized systems.
ref_texts.EU GMP Part II 5.46: 5.46 Incidents related to computerized systems that could affect the quality of intermediates or APIs or the reliability of records or test results should be recorded and investigated.
ref_texts.EU GMP Part II 5.47: 5.47 Changes to the computerized system should be made according to a change procedure and should be formally authorized, documented and tested. Records should be kept of all changes, including modifications and enhancements made to the hardware, software and any other critical component of the system. These records should demonstrate that the system is maintained in a validated state.

points.question: Is reaching the quality objective treated as the job of senior management, with staff, suppliers and distributors taking part?
points.verify: Verify that the attainment of the quality objective is the responsibility of senior management and has the participation and commitment of staff in different departments and at all levels within the company, the company's suppliers and the distributors.

evidence.what: quality system documents showing who is responsible for the quality objective
senior management and staff on their part in the quality objective

points.question: Is there a pharmaceutical quality system that includes GMP and quality risk management?
points.verify: Verify that, to achieve the quality objective reliably, there is a comprehensively designed and correctly implemented pharmaceutical quality system incorporating Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and Quality Risk Management (QRM).

evidence.what: description of the pharmaceutical quality system
records showing the quality system is implemented

points.question: Has senior management made sure a working quality system exists, has enough resources and has clear roles?
points.verify: Verify that senior management takes the ultimate responsibility to ensure that an effective pharmaceutical quality system is in place, is adequately resourced, and that roles, responsibilities and authorities are defined, communicated and implemented throughout the organisation.

evidence.what: documents defining roles, responsibilities and authorities
records showing these were communicated and implemented
senior management on resourcing of the quality system

points.question: Does senior management lead and actively take part in the quality system so that staff support it?
points.verify: Verify that senior management shows leadership and active participation in the pharmaceutical quality system, and that this ensures the support and commitment of staff at all levels and sites within the organisation to the pharmaceutical quality system.

evidence.what: records showing senior management participation in the quality system
staff at different levels on their commitment to the quality system

points.question: Does the quality system help innovation and continual improvement and tie development closer to manufacturing?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system (which may extend to the pharmaceutical development life-cycle stages) facilitates innovation and continual improvement and strengthens the link between pharmaceutical development and manufacturing activities.

evidence.what: quality system description
records showing improvements and links between development and manufacturing

points.question: Does every part of the quality system have enough resources and upkeep, including people, premises, equipment and facilities?
points.verify: Verify that all parts of the product quality system are adequately resourced and maintained, including being provided with sufficient competent personnel, suitable premises, equipment and facilities.

evidence.what: premises, equipment and facilities provided
records showing personnel numbers and competence

points.question: Do the quality system documents show that the manufacturer takes responsibility for the quality of its products?
points.verify: Verify that the manufacturer assumes responsibility for the quality of the pharmaceutical products to ensure that they are fit for their intended use, comply with the requirements of the licence and do not place patients at risk due to inadequate safety, quality or efficacy.

evidence.what: quality policy or quality manual stating the manufacturer's responsibility for product quality

points.question: Is the system for making products designed, qualified, planned, run, maintained and continuously improved so that quality is delivered consistently?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that product realisation is achieved by designing, qualifying, planning, implementing, maintaining and continuously improving a system that allows the consistent delivery of products with appropriate quality attributes.

evidence.what: quality system description
records showing the system is implemented, maintained and improved

points.question: Is knowledge about products and processes managed at every lifecycle stage?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that product and process knowledge is managed throughout all lifecycle stages.

evidence.what: procedure or documents on managing product and process knowledge
product and process knowledge records

points.question: Do product design and development consider GMP and the other GXPs?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that pharmaceutical products are designed and developed in a way that takes into account the requirements of GMP and other GXPs such as those of Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) and Good Clinical Practices (GCP).

evidence.what: product design and development documents

points.question: Are production and QC operations clearly written down, with GMP requirements adopted?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that production and quality control operations are clearly specified in a written form and GMP requirements are adopted.

evidence.what: written production and quality control instructions

points.question: Do job descriptions clearly state the responsibilities of managers?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that managerial responsibilities are clearly specified in the job descriptions.

evidence.what: job descriptions

points.question: Are there arrangements for correct starting and packaging materials, supplier selection and monitoring, and checking each delivery?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that arrangements are made for the manufacture, supply and use of the correct starting and packaging materials, the selection and monitoring of suppliers and for verifying that each delivery is the correct material from the approved supply chain.

evidence.what: procedures for materials, supplier selection and monitoring
records showing each delivery was verified

points.question: Are all needed controls on materials, intermediates and bulk, and other in-process controls, calibrations and validations done?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that all necessary controls on starting materials, intermediate products, and bulk products and other in-process controls, calibrations and validations are carried out.

evidence.what: control records for starting materials, intermediate and bulk products
in-process control, calibration and validation records

points.question: Is the finished product processed and checked correctly as the defined procedures say?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that the finished product is correctly processed and checked, according to the defined procedures.

evidence.what: defined procedures for processing and checking finished product
batch processing and checking records

points.question: Is every production batch certified by the authorised persons before it is sold or supplied?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that pharmaceutical products are not sold or supplied before the authorised persons have certified that each production batch has been produced and controlled in accordance with the requirements of the licence and other applicable regulations relevant to the production, control and release of pharmaceutical products.

evidence.what: batch certification records by authorised persons
sale or supply records

points.question: Are there processes to manage outsourced activities?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that processes are in place to ensure the management of outsourced activities.

evidence.what: procedures for managing outsourced activities
records showing outsourced activities are managed

points.question: Is there a self-inspection or quality audit procedure that regularly assesses the quality system?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that there is a procedure for self-inspection or quality audit that regularly appraises the effectiveness and applicability of the product quality system.

evidence.what: self-inspection or quality audit procedure
self-inspection or quality audit reports

points.question: Are monitoring results for product and processes used in batch release, deviation investigations and preventive action?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that product and processes are monitored and the results taken into account in batch release, in the investigation of deviations and with a view to taking preventive action to avoid potential deviations occurring in the future.

evidence.what: product and process monitoring results
batch release, deviation investigation and preventive action records

points.question: Are planned changes evaluated and approved before they are made, considering regulatory notification and approval?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that arrangements are in place for the prospective evaluation and approval of planned changes and their approval prior to their implementation, taking into account regulatory notification and approval where required.

evidence.what: arrangements for evaluating and approving planned changes
change records showing evaluation and approval before implementation

points.question: Is each change evaluated after it is made to confirm the aims were met with no unwanted quality effect?
points.verify: Verify that, after implementation of any change, an evaluation is undertaken to confirm that the quality objectives were achieved and that there was no unintended adverse impact on product quality.

evidence.what: evaluations done after implementation of changes

points.question: Are product quality reviews done regularly to check process consistency and find improvement needs?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that regular reviews of the quality of pharmaceutical products are conducted with the objective of verifying the consistency of the process and identifying where there is a need for improvement.

evidence.what: product quality review reports

points.question: Are quality improvements made that match current process and product knowledge?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that continual improvement is facilitated through the implementation of quality improvements appropriate to the current level of process and product knowledge.

evidence.what: records of quality improvements implemented

points.question: Is a quality risk management system in place?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that there is a system for QRM.

evidence.what: QRM system documents
QRM records

points.question: Are deviations, suspected defects and other problems reported, investigated and recorded, with root cause analysis?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that deviations, suspected product defects and other problems are reported, investigated and recorded, and that an appropriate level of root cause analysis is applied during such investigations.

evidence.what: deviation, suspected product defect and problem reports
investigation records showing root cause analysis

points.question: Do investigations name the most likely root causes, lead to corrective and preventive actions, and is their effectiveness followed?
points.verify: Verify that the most likely root causes are identified, that appropriate corrective and preventive actions are identified and taken, and that the effectiveness of corrective and preventive actions is monitored.

evidence.what: investigation records showing root causes
corrective and preventive action records and effectiveness monitoring

points.question: Does senior management take part in periodic reviews of the quality system, held at least yearly?
points.verify: Verify that there are periodic management reviews, with the involvement of senior management, of the operation of the product quality system to identify opportunities for continual improvement of products, processes and the system itself, and that, unless otherwise justified, such reviews are conducted at least annually.

evidence.what: management review records showing dates and senior management involvement
justification where reviews are not at least annual

points.question: Is the quality system defined and written down?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system is defined and documented.

evidence.what: quality system documentation

points.question: Is there a quality manual, or equivalent, that describes the quality management system and management responsibilities?
points.verify: Verify that a quality manual or an equivalent documentation is established and contains a description of the quality management system including management responsibilities.

evidence.what: quality manual or equivalent documentation

points.question: Do effective monitoring and control systems keep process performance and product quality in a state of control?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that a state of control is established and maintained by developing and using effective monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality.

evidence.what: monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality
process performance and product quality monitoring data

points.question: Does the quality system have satisfactory arrangements so that, as far as possible, products keep their quality in storage, distribution and later handling for their whole shelf-life?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that satisfactory arrangements exist to ensure, as far as possible, that the pharmaceutical products are stored, distributed and subsequently handled so that quality is maintained throughout their shelf-life.

evidence.what: storage, distribution and handling arrangements
storage of pharmaceutical products

points.question: Are quality risk evaluations based on science and process experience, and linked in the end to patient protection?
points.verify: Verify that Quality Risk Management ensures that the evaluation of the risk to quality is based on scientific knowledge, experience with the process and ultimately links to the protection of the patient.

evidence.what: quality risk assessments
QRM procedure

points.question: Does the effort, formality and paperwork of each risk exercise match the risk level?
points.verify: Verify that Quality Risk Management ensures the following: level of effort, formality and documentation of the QRM process is commensurate with the level of risk.

points.question: Does the MAH know it can help a site return to compliance for its own products (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH is aware of its ability to facilitate compliance, and that it may find its involvement in the remediation of such issues necessary, in relation to the products for which the MAH has responsibility (recommended).

evidence.what: MAH staff on their role in facilitating compliance

points.question: For manufacturers outside the EEA, is there valid proof of authorisation and of EU GMP compliance (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in the case of manufacturers located outside the EEA, there is a valid proof of authorisation (equivalent to MIA) where one is needed, and a valid EU GMP Certificate (or, where an MRA or equivalent applies, evidence of successful GMP inspection in relation to the product category / manufacturing activity of interest) (recommended).

evidence.what: proof of authorisation of manufacturers outside the EEA
EU GMP Certificate or evidence of successful GMP inspection

points.question: Has the MAH set up strong two-way communication with the authorities, the manufacturing sites, the QPs and the organisations that monitor quality after marketing (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH has established robust two-way communication systems with national competent authorities, manufacturing sites, Qualified Persons (QPs), and any organisations relevant to the monitoring of post-marketing quality (e.g. complaints processing and on-going stability monitoring) (recommended).

evidence.what: procedure or agreements showing the two-way communication systems
records showing communication in both directions with these parties

points.question: Can the manufacturing sites and QPs see what is registered in the marketing authorisation and any commitments agreed with the authorities (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the manufacturing sites and QPs have visibility of what is registered in the marketing authorisation and what, if any, regulatory commitments have been agreed with the competent authorities (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing registered details and regulatory commitments given to sites and QPs
QP: access to registered details and commitments

points.question: Does the MAH know the manufacturing processes, how impurities form, and the related controls at the product and active substance sites well enough (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH has adequate knowledge of the details of the manufacturing processes, including impurity formation, and their related controls at the finished product and active substance manufacturing sites (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing the process, impurity and control information held by the MAH
MAH staff: knowledge of processes and controls

points.question: Do records show that the MAH is kept informed of change management at the manufacturing sites, mainly changes that may affect the dossier, ASMFs or CEPs (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH is adequately informed of the change management activities at the manufacturing sites, particularly in relation to changes which may impact upon Modules 1, 2 and 3 / Parts 1 and 2 of the veterinary dossier, as well as on the contents of ASMFs and CEPs (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing site changes notified to the MAH

points.question: Do records show that the MAH tells the manufacturing sites about marketing authorisation changes that may affect them (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the manufacturing sites are adequately informed by the MAH of any MA changes which may have an impact on those sites, such as changes to the package leaflet, changes to specifications, etc. (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing MA changes notified by the MAH to the sites

points.question: Do the MAH and the manufacturer cooperate and exchange information in both directions, mainly on the registered details?
points.verify: Verify that there is cooperation between the MAH and manufacturer, and that two-way communication systems are in place between them, particularly in relation to what is registered in the MA.

evidence.what: description of communication systems between the MAH and the manufacturer
records of communication in both directions on what is registered in the MA

points.question: Do records show that manufacturing follows what was submitted and accepted in the MA application?
points.verify: Verify that the manufacturer ensures that all manufacturing operations for medicinal products subject to a marketing authorisation are carried out in accordance with the information provided in the application for marketing authorisation as accepted by the competent authorities.

evidence.what: records showing manufacturing operations follow the information in the accepted MA application

points.question: Where the manufacturer and the MAH are separate legal entities, do they cooperate so the manufacturer can meet GMP?
points.verify: Where the manufacturer and the marketing authorisation holder are different legal entities, verify that there is cooperation between them, so that the manufacturer is able to comply with those principles and guidelines (of good manufacturing practice).

evidence.what: records showing cooperation between the manufacturer and the MAH

points.question: Is there a technical agreement setting out what the manufacturer and the MAH owe each other (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the obligations of the manufacturer and marketing authorisation holder vis-à-vis each other are defined in a technical agreement between them (recommended).

evidence.what: technical agreement between the manufacturer and the MAH

points.question: Where the MAH and the manufacturer are separate legal entities, are their cooperation and communication written into a technical agreement (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that there is cooperation and communication between the MAH and manufacturer, when they are different legal entities, and that such arrangements are described in a technical agreement between the parties (recommended).

evidence.what: technical agreement between the parties
records of cooperation and communication between the MAH and the manufacturer

points.question: Does the MAH tell its manufacturers what is registered in the dossier, so that batches can be in line with the relevant MA (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH communicates to the manufacturers what is registered in the dossier, as manufacturers cannot comply with the GMP requirement for batches to be in line with the relevant MA unless the MAH does so (recommended).

evidence.what: communications from the MAH to manufacturers on what is registered in the dossier

points.question: Does the marketing authorisation give the needed radiation dose and its limits?
points.verify: Verify that the required dose, including justified limits, is stated in the marketing authorisation.

evidence.what: marketing authorisation

points.question: Has the MAH registered the irradiation dose details and passed them to the manufacturer?
points.verify: Verify that there is communication between the MAH and the manufacturer in relation to the strength and limits of the irradiating dose. Verify that the MAH ensures that this information is registered in the marketing authorisation and communicates what has been registered with the manufacturer, so that the manufacturer may maintain compliance with the marketing authorisation.

evidence.what: marketing authorisation
records of communication between the MAH and the manufacturer on the strength and limits of the irradiating dose

points.question: Where an ASMF is used for a human medicine, has the active substance maker given the applicant the data it needs?
points.verify: Where an Active Substance Master File is supplied directly to the competent authorities by the manufacturer of the active substance, verify that the manufacturer provides the applicant with all of the data which may be necessary for the latter to take responsibility for the medicinal product.

evidence.what: data provided by the active substance manufacturer to the applicant

points.question: Is there a written confirmation from the active substance maker on consistency and on not changing without telling the applicant?
points.verify: Verify that the manufacturer has confirmed in writing to the applicant that he shall ensure batch to batch consistency and not modify the manufacturing process or specifications without informing the applicant.

evidence.what: written confirmation from the manufacturer to the applicant

points.question: Are the supporting papers for such a change sent to the authorities, and to the applicant for the open part?
points.verify: Verify that documents and particulars supporting the application for such a change are supplied to the competent authorities, and that these documents and particulars are also supplied to the applicant when they concern the open part of the active substance master file.

evidence.what: records of documents and particulars supplied to the competent authorities and to the applicant

points.question: Where a granted certificate of suitability exists, is it placed in the right part of Module 3?
points.verify: Where the active substance and/or a raw and starting material or excipient(s) are the subject of a monograph of the European Pharmacopoeia and the applicant has applied for a certificate of suitability (which the applicant can do), verify that the certificate, where granted by the European Directorate for the Quality of Medicines, is presented in the relevant section of this Module (i.e. Module 3).

evidence.what: Module 3 of the dossier

points.question: Has the manufacturer assured the applicant in writing that the process is unchanged since the certificate of suitability was granted?
points.verify: Verify that the manufacturer has given the assurance in writing to the applicant that the manufacturing process has not been modified since the granting of the certificate of suitability by the European Directorate for the Quality of Medicines.

evidence.what: written assurance from the manufacturer to the applicant

points.question: Where an ASMF is used for a veterinary medicine, has the active substance maker given the applicant its part of the file?
points.verify: Where the information on the active substance is supplied directly to the competent authorities by the manufacturer of the active substance as an Active Substance Master File, verify that the manufacturer of the active substance provides the applicant with all the data (applicant's part of the Active Substance Master File) which may be necessary for the latter to take responsibility for the veterinary medicinal product.

evidence.what: applicant's part of the Active Substance Master File provided to the applicant

points.question: Does the product dossier hold a copy of the data the active substance maker gave the applicant?
points.verify: Verify that a copy of the data provided by the active substance manufacturer to the applicant is included in the medicinal product dossier.

evidence.what: medicinal product dossier

points.question: For a veterinary medicine, is there a written confirmation from the active substance maker on consistency and on not changing without telling the applicant?
points.verify: Verify that the manufacturer of the active substance has confirmed in writing to the applicant that he shall ensure batch-to-batch consistency and not modify the manufacturing process or specifications without informing the applicant.

evidence.what: written confirmation from the active substance manufacturer to the applicant

points.question: Where the veterinary dossier refers to a certificate of suitability, is there a written assurance that the process is unchanged since it was granted?
points.verify: Where a certificate of suitability is referred to, verify that the manufacturer has given an assurance in writing to the applicant that the manufacturing process has not been modified since the granting of the certificate of suitability by the European Directorate for the Quality of Medicines and HealthCare.

evidence.what: written assurance from the manufacturer to the applicant

points.question: Can the MAH, together with the finished product maker, get all relevant information on how the active substance is made now?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH ensures that it, in conjunction with the finished product manufacturer, has access to all relevant information concerning the current manufacture of the active substance.

evidence.what: information held on the current manufacture of the active substance
arrangements giving access to that information

points.question: Are working communication routes in place between the parties about active substance manufacture?
points.verify: Verify that effective communication processes are in place between the concerned parties in relation to the manufacture of the active substance.

evidence.what: description of communication processes between the concerned parties
records of communication on the manufacture of the active substance

points.question: Does the MA applicant or MAH hold or have access to the open part of the ASMF, also when a CEP is used?
points.verify: Verify that the MA applicant/MAH has access to the open part (or its equivalent) of the ASMF, including when a CEP is used.

evidence.what: open part (or its equivalent) of the ASMF available to the MA applicant/MAH

points.question: For an aseptically made active substance, are the full sterilization step details given to the finished product maker and placed in the dossier?
points.verify: In the case of an aseptically manufactured active substance, verify that full information on the sterilization step is made available to the finished product manufacturer, and that it is included in Module 3/Part II of the MA dossier (the inclusion in the dossier is a recommendation: 'should').

evidence.what: information on the sterilization step provided to the finished product manufacturer
Module 3/Part II of the MA dossier

points.question: Has the MA applicant or MAH made sure it can get all the relevant information (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MA applicant/MAH ensures that they have access to all the relevant information (recommended).

evidence.what: arrangements giving the MA applicant/MAH access to the relevant information

points.question: Do the communication routes also cover planned changes to the active substance process or specifications (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that such communication processes also address proposed changes in the manufacturing process or specifications, to enable the MAH to assess the implications of the proposed change on the finished product and to apply for any required variations to the MA, in accordance with the EU Variation Classification Guideline (recommended).

evidence.what: description of communication processes covering proposed changes
records of proposed changes communicated to the MAH

points.question: Where a CEP is registered, does the MAH still have a QP-signed GMP declaration for the active substance maker?
points.verify: If a CEP for an active substance is registered in an MA, verify that the MAH still has available a declaration of GMP (signed by the Qualified Person) relating to the GMP compliance status of the active substance manufacturer.

evidence.what: declaration of GMP signed by the Qualified Person

points.question: Does the MAH know enough about how the active substance is made and controlled to answer for product quality (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the level of knowledge that the MAH has in relation to the manufacture and control of the active substance is such that it permits the MAH to take responsibility for the quality of the medicinal product, and that this is not less than when there is an ASMF registered in the MA (recommended).

evidence.what: information held by the MAH on the manufacture and control of the active substance
MAH staff on the manufacture and control of the active substance

points.question: Has the MAH or applicant made sure these points are clearly covered, by a technical agreement if needed (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH (or applicant) ensures that the above requirements are clearly addressed, and if necessary via a technical agreement between the MAH and the active substance manufacturer (recommended).

evidence.what: technical agreement or other document between the MAH and the active substance manufacturer addressing these requirements

points.question: Is care taken over how documents are made, checked and issued (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that documents are designed, prepared, reviewed, and distributed with care (recommended).

evidence.what: documents as designed, prepared, reviewed and distributed
records of preparation, review and distribution of documents

points.question: Do documents agree with the product specification files and the authorisation dossiers (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that documents comply with the relevant parts of Product Specification Files, Manufacturing and Marketing Authorisation dossiers, as appropriate (recommended).

evidence.what: documents compared with Product Specification Files, Manufacturing and Marketing Authorisation dossiers

points.question: Are working copies made from master documents free from copying errors (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the reproduction of working documents from master documents does not allow any error to be introduced through the reproduction process (recommended).

evidence.what: working documents compared with their master documents
how working documents are reproduced from master documents

points.question: Do the registered-detail documents the MAH gives to sites match the MA?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH ensures that any documents that it provides to the manufacturing sites relating to what is registered in the MA accurately reflect the relevant parts of the MA.

evidence.what: documents provided by the MAH to the manufacturing sites compared with the relevant parts of the MA

points.question: Do labels and leaflets match the MA, and are their variations passed to the site promptly (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that documents relating to the registered product information intended for the patient or user of the medicine (i.e. labels and leaflets) are in line with the marketing authorisation, and that changes (variations) to these items are communicated to the manufacturing site in a timely manner (recommended).

evidence.what: labels and leaflets compared with the marketing authorisation
records of communication of label and leaflet variations to the manufacturing site

points.question: Do the MAH and the relevant sites talk often and effectively (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that there are effective and frequent communications between the MAH and the relevant manufacturing sites; this is not just in relation to what is registered in the MA, but it might also concern the results of Product Quality Reviews (PQRs), information about regulatory commitments, proposed changes which may affect Modules 1, 2 and 3 / Parts 1 and 2 of the MA, among other things (recommended).

evidence.what: records of communications between the MAH and the relevant manufacturing sites

points.question: Was supply chain complexity taken into account when deciding which communication processes are needed (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that complexity in relation to the supply chain is considered when determining what communication processes need to be in place; this can relate to the number and type of different manufacturers in the supply chain, the degree of outsourcing that is in place, the geographic spread of the various actors in the supply chain, etc. (recommended).

evidence.what: documents or records showing how the needed communication processes were determined

points.question: Where group companies describe their communication only in SOPs, are those SOPs approved by both sides and named in the technical agreement (recommended)?
points.verify: In cases where the MAH and the manufacturer are part of the same overall group of companies and SOPs are used to document how the actual communication processes are expected to work (which may be sufficient), verify that those SOPs are approved by both parties and that they are referred to within the technical agreement between the parties (recommended).

evidence.what: SOPs on the communication processes
technical agreement between the parties

points.question: Where the MAH and the manufacturer are not in the same group, are communication duties written into agreements or contracts (recommended)?
points.verify: In other situations, where the MAH and the manufacturer are not part of the same overall group of companies, verify that the communication processes and responsibilities are documented in technical agreements or in contracts, as they may be more complex and at a higher risk of failing (recommended).

evidence.what: technical agreements or contracts between the MAH and the manufacturer

points.question: Does information on planned changes, suspected defects and possible recalls pass both ways between the parties (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that there is a two-way flow of information between the parties, especially in the context of proposed changes which may require variation applications or regulatory notifications to the competent authority by the MAH, and also with regard to suspected quality defects and potential recall issues which may have been reported to one or other party, but not to both, and which may need to be reported onwards to the competent authority (recommended).

evidence.what: records of information exchanged between the parties on proposed changes
records of information exchanged on suspected quality defects and potential recall issues

points.question: Are communication processes and systems kept up carefully for as long as the product or the relationship lasts (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that communication processes and systems are maintained with care, extending over the product life-cycle (e.g. during the licensing procedure, commercial manufacture, the fulfilment of regulatory commitments, the submission and implementation of post-approval variations, etc.) or at least up until the end of the relationship between the concerned parties (recommended).

evidence.what: description of communication processes and systems
records showing the communication processes and systems are maintained

points.question: Do the MAH's communication systems keep it informed of everything happening with the product concerned (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH ensures that communication systems are in place which will enable it to keep abreast of all developments, changes and commitments relating to the specific product of concern (recommended).

evidence.what: description of the MAH's communication systems
records of developments, changes and commitments received by the MAH for the product

points.question: For manufacturing-related variations, does the MAH inform the authority of amendments to what was submitted?
points.verify: In relation to manufacturing-related MA variations, verify that the MAH, as its responsibility via Directive 2001/83/EC and Regulation 2019/6, provides the competent authority with information on amendments relative to the information submitted in the dossier.

evidence.what: records of information on amendments provided to the competent authority

points.question: Is new information that could change the registered particulars sent to the national authority without delay?
points.verify: Verify that, as the Directive states (Ref. Directive 2001/83/EC, Article 23 (2)), the marketing authorisation holder forthwith provides the national competent authority with any new information which might entail the amendment of the particulars or documents referred to in Article 8(3), Articles 10, 10a, 10b and 11, or Article 32(5), or Annex I.

evidence.what: records of new information provided to the national competent authority

points.question: Has the MAH set up ways of communicating with manufacturing sites and other parties so that it stays informed of scientific and technical developments and can discuss initiatives?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH has communication systems in place with manufacturing sites and other parties which enable it to keep abreast of scientific and technical progress and advances and to discuss initiatives in this area.

evidence.what: procedure or agreement describing the communication systems with manufacturing sites and other parties
records of communication on scientific and technical progress and initiatives

points.question: Does the authorisation holder follow scientific and technical progress for its registered manufacturing and control methods and make the changes needed so that the product is made and checked by generally accepted scientific methods?
points.verify: Verify that, after an authorisation has been issued, the authorisation holder, in respect of the methods of manufacture and control provided for in the application, takes account of scientific and technical progress and introduces any changes that may be required to enable the medicinal product to be manufactured and checked by means of generally accepted scientific methods (Article 23 of Directive 2001/83/EC).

evidence.what: records showing scientific and technical progress was taken into account for the methods of manufacture and control
records of changes introduced to the methods of manufacture and control

points.question: Do the MAH's copies of the registered dossier parts (and the manufacturer's, if applicable) get updated whenever a document or section in them is changed?
points.verify: Verify that the copies of these CTD Modules / Parts 1 and 2 as held by the MAH (and by the manufacturer, if applicable) are continually kept updated, by replacing individual documents or Sections within a Module with the updated versions, as changes are made to those documents or sections within that Module.

evidence.what: copies of the CTD Modules / Parts 1 and 2 held by the MAH (and by the manufacturer, if applicable)
records showing changed documents or sections were replaced with the updated versions

points.question: Do the manufacturer and, where different, the MAH evaluate the quality review results and assess whether corrective and preventive action or revalidation is needed (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the manufacturer and, where different, the marketing authorisation holder evaluate the results of the review and that an assessment is made as to whether corrective and preventive action or any revalidation should be undertaken, under the Pharmaceutical Quality System (recommended).

evidence.what: records of evaluation of the review results by the manufacturer and, where different, the MAH
records of the assessment of whether corrective and preventive action or revalidation should be undertaken

points.question: Are there management procedures to manage and review these actions on an ongoing basis, and is their effectiveness verified in self-inspection (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that there are management procedures for the ongoing management and review of these actions and that the effectiveness of these procedures is verified during self-inspection (recommended).

evidence.what: management procedures for ongoing management and review of the actions
self-inspection records showing the effectiveness of these procedures was verified

points.question: Where quality reviews are grouped by product type, is the grouping scientifically justified (recommended)?
points.verify: Where quality reviews are grouped by product type (e.g. solid dosage forms, liquid dosage forms, sterile products, etc.), verify that the grouping is scientifically justified (recommended).

evidence.what: grouped quality reviews and the scientific justification for the grouping

points.question: Where the MAH is not the manufacturer, does a technical agreement between the parties set out who does what in producing the product quality review (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where the marketing authorisation holder is not the manufacturer, there is a technical agreement in place between the various parties that defines their respective responsibilities in producing the product quality review (recommended).

evidence.what: technical agreement between the parties defining responsibilities in producing the product quality review

points.question: Does the MAH, when it is not the product manufacturer, itself evaluate the PQR results and assess the need for CAPAs and revalidation?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH, when it is not the product manufacturer, evaluates the results of the PQR and makes an assessment in relation to the need for corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs) and revalidation activities. Verify that the MAH performs this PQR evaluation and assessment work as its primary responsibility in relation to PQR activities.

evidence.what: MAH records of evaluation of the PQR results
MAH records of the assessment of the need for CAPAs and revalidation activities

points.question: Do records show that both parties, the MAH and the manufacturer, each did the PQR evaluation and assessment?
points.verify: Verify that both parties do the evaluation of the results of the PQR and the assessment in relation to the need for corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs) and revalidation activities.

evidence.what: PQR evaluation and assessment records of both parties

points.question: Is the PQR evaluation and assessment work overseen through both ongoing management review and self-inspection?
points.verify: Verify that oversight is applied to the PQR evaluation and assessment activities in two different ways: ongoing management review and self-inspection processes.

evidence.what: management review records covering the PQR evaluation and assessment activities
self-inspection records covering the PQR evaluation and assessment activities

points.question: Does the MAH keep its PQR evaluation and assessment work with itself and not hand it over to the manufacturer (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH does not delegate its evaluation and assessment work to the manufacturer (recommended).

evidence.what: agreement or procedure showing who does the MAH's PQR evaluation and assessment work
PQR evaluation and assessment records showing who did the MAH's work

points.question: Where stability results from an outsourced third party come to the MAH and not directly to the manufacturer, does the MAH see that the relevant stability data are in the PQR and adequately reviewed (recommended)?
points.verify: Where the MAH has outsourced the storage and/or testing of the stability samples to a third party which is not the product manufacturer and the results are sent to the MAH and not directly to the manufacturer, verify that the MAH ensures that the relevant stability data are included in the PQR and that the data are subject to an adequate review (recommended).

evidence.what: PQR showing the relevant stability data included
records showing the stability data were reviewed

points.question: Is the MAH's role in PQRs set out as different from the manufacturer's role (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH's role in relation to PQRs is different from that of the manufacturer (recommended).

evidence.what: procedure or agreement describing the roles of the MAH and the manufacturer in relation to PQRs

points.question: Does the PQR contain the MAH's own information on complaints, recalls, MA variations and other changes, and post-marketing commitments (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the information held by the MAH that is included in the PQR covers, for example, information relating to product complaints which the MAH may have received directly from the marketplace and which may not also have been sent directly to the manufacturer, as well as information about product recalls, MA variations and other changes, as well as post-marketing commitments (recommended).

evidence.what: PQR report sections on complaints, recalls, MA variations and other changes, post-marketing commitments
MAH records of complaints, recalls, variations and other changes, post-marketing commitments

points.question: Do the MAH and the distributors keep up appropriate and continued supply of the marketed product so that patients' needs in the Member State are covered?
points.verify: Verify that the holder of a marketing authorisation for a medicinal product and the distributors of that medicinal product actually placed on the market in a Member State, within the limits of their responsibilities, ensure appropriate and continued supplies of that medicinal product to pharmacies and persons authorised to supply medicinal products so that the needs of patients in the Member State in question are covered (Article 81 of Directive 2001/83/EC).

evidence.what: records showing appropriate and continued supplies to pharmacies and persons authorised to supply medicinal products in the Member State

points.question: For veterinary medicinal products, does the MAH keep up appropriate and continued supply of its products?
points.verify: Verify that, for veterinary medicinal products, the marketing authorisation holder, within the limits of its responsibilities, ensures appropriate and continued supplies of its veterinary medicinal products (Regulation 2019/6, Article 58 (2)).

evidence.what: records showing appropriate and continued supplies of the veterinary medicinal products

points.question: Does the MAH also follow any national rules within the EEA on keeping products in supply (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH also complies with any national requirements that may exist within the EEA in relation to maintaining product supply (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing compliance with national requirements within the EEA on maintaining product supply

points.question: Do records show that the MAH reports supply restrictions to the relevant competent authorities?
points.verify: Verify that, in accordance with Chapter 5 of the GMP Guide, the MAH reports restrictions in supply to the relevant competent authorities.

evidence.what: reports of restrictions in supply sent by the MAH to the relevant competent authorities

points.question: Does the manufacturer tell the MAH in good time about manufacturing constraints that could cause an abnormal supply restriction (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the manufacturer reports to the marketing authorisation holder (MAH) any constraints in manufacturing operations which may result in abnormal restriction in the supply, and that this is done in a timely manner to facilitate reporting of the restriction in supply by the MAH, to the relevant competent authorities, in accordance with its legal obligations (recommended).

evidence.what: manufacturer's reports to the MAH of constraints in manufacturing operations, with dates

points.question: Has the MAH made sure that how it and the manufacturer communicate on potential supply issues is agreed and clearly written in a technical agreement (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH ensures that the communication arrangements between it and the manufacturer on potential supply issues are agreed and clearly documented in a technical agreement between the parties (recommended).

evidence.what: technical agreement between the MAH and the manufacturer with the communication arrangements on potential supply issues

points.question: Where the two companies belong to the same overall organisation and the practical communication details are in SOPs, are those SOPs approved by both parties and referred to in the technical agreement (recommended)?
points.verify: Where the two companies are part of the same overall organisation and the specific details in relation to how the communications processes are intended to work at a practical level are documented in SOPs, verify that those SOPs are approved by both parties and that they are referred to within the technical agreement between the parties (recommended).

evidence.what: SOPs on the communications processes, showing approval by both parties
technical agreement between the parties referring to those SOPs

points.question: Besides internal supply chain information, does the MAH also take into account supply problem alerts from outside sources such as wholesalers, pharmacies and hospitals (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in addition to information from the internal supply chain, alerts on supply problems issued by e.g. wholesalers, pharmacies and hospitals are also considered by the MAH (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing alerts on supply problems from e.g. wholesalers, pharmacies and hospitals were considered by the MAH

points.question: When a product stops being marketed in a Member State, does the MAH notify that State's competent authority at least two months before, other than in exceptional circumstances?
points.verify: Verify that, if the product ceases to be placed on the market of a Member State, either temporarily or permanently, the MAH notifies the competent authority of that Member State, as required via Article 23a of Directive 2001/83/EC. Verify that such notifications are, other than in exceptional circumstances, made no less than two months before the interruption in the placing on the market of the product.

evidence.what: notifications to the competent authority of the Member State, with dates
records showing the date of the interruption in the placing on the market

points.question: Does the MAH tell the authorities at once, with reasons, when it suspends marketing, withdraws a product, asks for withdrawal of an authorisation or does not apply for its renewal?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH informs the competent authority of the reasons for such action in accordance with Article 123(2) of the Directive. Verify that the MAH notifies the Member States concerned forthwith of any action taken by the MAH to suspend the marketing of a medicinal product, to withdraw a medicinal product from the market, to request the withdrawal of a marketing authorisation or not to apply for the renewal of a marketing authorisation, together with the reasons for such action.

evidence.what: notifications to the competent authority and the Member States concerned, with dates and the reasons given

points.question: For a veterinary product, does the MAH inform the authority without delay, before acting and with reasons, of any step it plans to take to stop marketing?
points.verify: Verify that the marketing authorisation holder without delay informs the competent authority which has granted the marketing authorisation or the Commission, as applicable, of any action which the holder intends to take in order to cease the marketing of a veterinary medicinal product prior to taking such action, together with the reasons for such action.

evidence.what: information sent to the competent authority or the Commission, with dates and the reasons given
records showing the date the action to cease marketing was taken

points.question: Has the MAH done proactive and detailed risk assessments of its manufacturing, regulatory and supply chain processes and worked on the weaknesses found (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH carries out, in line with quality risk management principles, proactive and detailed risk assessments of its manufacturing, regulatory and supply chain processes, and works to address any identified weaknesses in those areas (recommended).

evidence.what: risk assessments of the manufacturing, regulatory and supply chain processes
records of work to address the identified weaknesses

points.question: Besides preventing shortages, does the MAH have a risk management protocol ready to reduce the impact if a supply disruption happens (recommended)?

points.question: Are sterile processes and their monitoring systems handled by people with the right process, engineering and microbiology knowledge (recommended)?

points.question: Are raw and packaging materials controlled and tested so that their bioburden and endotoxin/pyrogen levels suit their use (recommended)?

points.question: Is the combined effectiveness of the contamination control measures looked at together (recommended)?

points.question: Does the CCS cover every aspect of contamination control and is it reviewed on an ongoing and periodic basis (recommended)?

knowledge of products, equipment and methods
