points.verify: Verify that the manufacturing authorisation holder has a series of strategies ranging from acceptance through control to unacceptable for the different risk profiles and that, based on these, a control strategy, e.g. audit, document retrieval and testing, is established (recommended).

evidence.what: strategies for the different risk profiles
established control strategy

points.question: Is there ongoing risk review using defect data and quality trends of the excipient (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, once the appropriate GMP for the excipient and the risk profile of the excipient manufacturer have been defined, ongoing risk review is performed through mechanisms such as: number of defects connected to batches of excipient received; type/severity of such defects; monitoring and trend analysis of excipient quality (recommended).

evidence.what: ongoing risk review records for excipients

points.question: Does ongoing risk review use loss of certification, drug product trends and changes at the excipient maker (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, once the appropriate GMP for the excipient and the risk profile of the excipient manufacturer have been defined, ongoing risk review is performed through mechanisms such as: loss of relevant quality system and/or GMP certification by excipient manufacturer; observation of trends in drug product quality attributes, which will depend on the nature and role of excipient; observed organisational, procedural or technical/process changes at the excipient manufacturer (recommended).

evidence.what: ongoing risk review records for excipients

points.question: Does ongoing risk review use audits or questionnaires of the excipient maker (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, once the appropriate GMP for the excipient and the risk profile of the excipient manufacturer have been defined, ongoing risk review is performed through mechanisms such as: audit/re-audit of excipient manufacturer; questionnaires (recommended).

evidence.what: ongoing risk review records for excipients

points.question: Is the control strategy looked at again after each risk review and changed when needed (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, based on the outcome of the risk review, the established control strategy is reviewed and revised if needed (recommended).

evidence.what: review and revision of the control strategy

points.question: Is each delegation of MAH tasks and activities written down and agreed by the parties (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that any delegation of the tasks and activities which relate to the MAH's responsibilities is described in writing and agreed by the relevant parties (recommended).

evidence.what: written delegation agreed by the relevant parties

points.question: Does the MAH make sure that whoever takes on a delegated task is able and informed enough to do it?
points.verify: Verify that, in general terms, the MAH ensures that the person or entity, to whom any task or activity has been delegated, possesses the required competence, information and knowledge to successfully carry out the outsourced activities (Ref: GMP Guide Chapter 7, Paragraphs 7.5 and 7.6).

evidence.what: records showing competence, information and knowledge of the delegated party

points.question: Where tasks are spread over more than one party, is special attention given (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that special attention is given to situations where tasks have been delegated in a fragmented way - to more than one party - as applying oversight of multiple parties can be a challenge in the life-cycle management of the medicinal product (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing attention to tasks delegated to more than one party
MAH staff overseeing delegated tasks

points.question: Is each outsourced activity set out in a written document?
points.verify: Verify that outsourced activities are described in writing.

evidence.what: written descriptions of outsourced activities

points.question: Where the MAH is not the manufacturer, are suitable arrangements in place between them (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where the marketing authorization holder and the manufacturer are not the same, appropriate arrangements are in place, taking into account the principles described in this chapter (Chapter 7 of the GMP Guide) (recommended).

evidence.what: arrangements between MAH and manufacturer

points.question: Are the arrangements between the parties written into technical agreements in every scenario (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, regardless of the scenario that applies, the arrangements between the parties are documented in technical agreements (recommended).

evidence.what: technical agreements between the parties

points.question: Has the MAH put in writing what each outsourced activity is and how it is controlled (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where an MAH is engaged in an outsourcing activity, the MAH agrees in writing what exactly the activity is, and how it will be controlled (recommended).

evidence.what: written agreement on the outsourced activity and its control

points.question: Is every outsourced activity defined, agreed and controlled so that misunderstandings are avoided?
points.verify: Verify that, as Chapter 7 of the GMP Guide requires, any activity that is outsourced is appropriately defined, agreed and controlled in order to avoid misunderstandings which could result in a product or operation of unsatisfactory quality.

evidence.what: agreements defining outsourced activities
records showing control of outsourced activities

points.question: Where outsourced work could affect MA compliance, are controls in place to assure it (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, if an outsourced activity is one that may affect compliance with the MA, there are controls in place which provide assurance that the requirements of the MA are complied with (recommended).

evidence.what: controls for outsourced activities affecting MA compliance
records showing these controls are in place

points.question: Do outsourcing arrangements and proposed changes to them follow the regulations and the product's MA (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that all arrangements for the outsourced activities including any proposed changes in technical or other arrangements are in accordance with regulations in force, and the Marketing Authorisation for the product concerned, where applicable (recommended).

evidence.what: arrangements for outsourced activities and proposed changes
Marketing Authorisation for the product concerned

points.question: Does the technical agreement say who does what for the product quality review when manufacture is outsourced (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where manufacture is outsourced, the technical agreement between MAH and manufacturer addresses the respective responsibilities in producing and evaluating the product quality review (recommended).

evidence.what: technical agreement between MAH and manufacturer

points.question: Do the controls that assure MA compliance for outsourced activities also cover post-approval changes and how they are implemented (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the controls for outsourced activities which provide assurance that the requirements of the MA are complied with also cover activities concerning post-approval changes and their implementation (recommended).

evidence.what: procedure or agreement describing the controls on outsourced activities for post-approval changes

points.question: Are the critical documents behind the Marketing Authorisation kept for as long as it is in force (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that critical documentation, including raw data (for example relating to validation or stability), which supports information in the Marketing Authorisation is retained whilst the authorisation remains in force (recommended).

evidence.what: document retention procedure
retained critical documentation and raw data

points.question: Can the MAH show it is satisfied with how the manufacturer retains documentation (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH is satisfied with the documentation retention policies and practices that are in place at the manufacturer (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing the MAH is satisfied with the manufacturer's retention policies and practices

points.question: Does the agreement or contract between the parties cover document retention arrangements (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the documentation retention arrangements are addressed in a technical agreement or a contract between the parties, whichever may apply (recommended).

evidence.what: technical agreement or contract

points.question: Where superseded documentation is retired, is there a written justification that respects batch record retention (recommended)?
points.verify: Where certain documentation (e.g. raw data supporting validation reports or stability reports) is retired because the data has been superseded by a full set of new data, verify that the justification is documented and takes into account the requirements for retention of batch documentation; for example, for process validation data, the accompanying raw data is retained for a period at least as long as the records for all batches whose release has been supported on the basis of that validation exercise (recommended).

evidence.what: documented justification for retiring documentation
retained raw data and batch records

points.question: Is batch documentation of investigational products kept long enough after the last clinical trial?
points.verify: Verify that, for investigational medicinal products for human use, the batch documentation is retained for at least five years after the completion or formal discontinuation of the last clinical trial in which the batch was used.

evidence.what: retention procedure for batch documentation
retained batch documentation

points.question: Does the sponsor or MAH make sure records needed for a later marketing authorisation are kept?
points.verify: Verify that the sponsor or marketing authorisation holder, if different, takes responsibility for ensuring that records are retained as required for marketing authorisation in accordance with the Annex I to Directive 2001/83/EC, if required for a subsequent marketing authorisation.

evidence.what: procedure or agreement showing who ensures record retention
retained records

points.question: Have the parties agreed who does what for record retention (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that record retention responsibilities and activities are agreed between the manufacturer, MAH or sponsor (recommended).

evidence.what: agreement on record retention responsibilities and activities

points.question: For outsourced manufacture, does the technical agreement say who prepares and who assesses the product quality review (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where manufacture is outsourced, the technical agreement between MAH and manufacturer addresses the respective responsibilities in producing and evaluating the product quality review (recommended).

evidence.what: technical agreement between MAH and manufacturer

points.question: Does the MAH have a technical agreement covering its role in sourcing human derived starting materials?
points.verify: Verify that, in relation to the manufacture of biological active substances and medicinal products for human use, the MAH has a technical agreement in place with other parties which describes its responsibilities relating to the sourcing of human derived starting materials for biological products.

evidence.what: technical agreement between the MAH and other parties

points.question: For human tissues and cells used as starting materials, does a technical agreement set out each party's tasks (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, as the GMP Guide states (Ref. Annex 2, Paragraph 36(g)), for human tissues and cells used as starting materials for biological medicinal products, a technical agreement is in place between the responsible parties (e.g. manufacturers, tissue establishment, Sponsors, MA Holder) which defines the tasks of each party, including the RP [Responsible Person] and Qualified Person (recommended).

evidence.what: technical agreement between the responsible parties

points.question: Has the MAH agreed with the manufacturer the irradiation cycle design and the keeping of cycle records?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH has agreed the design of irradiation cycles with the manufacturer and has agreed how and where irradiation cycle records are retained.

evidence.what: agreement between MAH and manufacturer on irradiation cycle design and record retention

points.question: Where the dose is planned over several exposures or passes, has the MAH agreed and is a time period fixed in advance (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, when the radiation dose needed is by design given during more than one exposure or passage through the plant, this is with the agreement of the holder of the marketing authorisation and occurs within a predetermined time period (recommended).

evidence.what: agreement of the marketing authorisation holder and the predetermined time period
irradiation records showing exposures or passages and their timing

points.question: Is the MAH told about unplanned stops that push irradiation past the agreed period (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that unplanned interruptions during irradiation are notified to the holder of the marketing authorisation if this extends the irradiation process beyond a previously agreed period (recommended).

evidence.what: irradiation records showing unplanned interruptions
notifications to the marketing authorisation holder

points.question: Are the records of each irradiation batch checked, signed by a named responsible person and kept (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that process and control records for each irradiation batch are checked and signed by a nominated responsible person and retained (recommended).

evidence.what: process and control records for irradiation batches

points.question: Have the plant operator and the MAH agreed how and where irradiation batch records are kept (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the method and place of retention of the process and control records are agreed between the plant operator and the holder of the marketing authorisation (recommended).

evidence.what: agreement between plant operator and marketing authorisation holder on record retention

points.question: Does the MAH of a product processed with ionising radiation refer to the CPMP guidance on this subject?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH of a product which includes ionising radiation in its processing refers to the CPMP guidance on 'Ionising radiation in the manufacture of medicinal products'.

evidence.what: MAH documents showing reference to the CPMP guidance

points.question: Is the MAH able to understand and technically judge how irradiation cycles are designed?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH is in a position to understand and to technically assess the design of irradiation cycles.

evidence.what: MAH staff on the design of irradiation cycles
records showing the MAH's assessment of irradiation cycle design

points.question: Does the MAH itself keep the task of working on irradiation cycle design, without passing it to the product manufacturer?
points.verify: Verify that the direct requirement for the MAH to work with the manufacturer with regard to the design of irradiation cycles is not delegated by the MAH to the manufacturer of the medicinal product.

evidence.what: technical agreement showing delegated tasks
records showing the MAH's work on irradiation cycle design

points.question: Where the MAH and the batch release site are different legal entities, does a written agreement say who takes and stores the samples (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where the marketing authorisation holder is not the same legal entity as the site(s) responsible for batch release within the EEA, the responsibility for taking and storage of reference/retention samples is defined in a written agreement between the two parties in accordance with Chapter 7 of the EC Guide to Good Manufacturing Practice (recommended).

evidence.what: written agreement between MAH and batch release site(s)

points.question: Where other sites do manufacturing or batch release work, do written agreements between the sites cover sample taking and keeping (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, also where any manufacturing or batch release activity is carried out at a site other than that with overall responsibility for the batch on the EEA market, the arrangements between each different site for the taking and keeping of reference and retention samples are defined in a written agreement (recommended).

evidence.what: written agreements between the different sites

points.question: Where sample arrangements are handed to another manufacturer, does the MAH handle the delegation and inform the authority?
points.verify: Where the manufacturer is not in a position to make the necessary arrangements and this is delegated to another manufacturer (which is allowed), verify that the Marketing Authorisation holder takes responsibility for such delegation and for the provision of all necessary information to the Competent Authority.

evidence.what: delegation arrangement with the other manufacturer
information provided to the Competent Authority

points.question: Has the MAH consulted each concerned Member State authority on whether the proposed sample storage is suitable (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH, in relation to the suitability of the proposed arrangements for storage of reference and retention samples, consults with the competent authority of each Member State in which any unexpired batch has been placed on the market (recommended).

evidence.what: consultation with the competent authorities

points.question: Has the MAH agreed with its manufacturers how reference and retention samples are taken and stored, as Annex 19 states?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH meets the responsibilities that Annex 19 states for the MAH in this area, mainly in relation to agreeing with the relevant manufacturers the arrangements for the taking and storage of reference and retention samples.

evidence.what: agreement between MAH and manufacturers on reference and retention samples

points.question: Is the finished product manufacturer suitably qualified to check the GMP status of the active substance makers?
points.verify: Verify that the finished product manufacturer is suitably qualified in order to be able to verify, for the applicant and the MAH, the GMP compliance status of the active substance manufacturer(s), as required in legislation.

evidence.what: records showing the finished product manufacturer is suitably qualified for this verification

points.question: Does the MA application include the QP Declaration on the GMP status of the active substance manufacturer?
points.verify: Verify that the applicant provides in the MA application information concerning the GMP compliance status of the manufacturer of the active substance, with reference to audits of that manufacturer, as a written confirmation (QP Declaration) that the manufacturer of the medicinal product has verified compliance of the manufacturer of the active substance with the principles and guidelines of good manufacturing practice by conducting audits, in accordance with point (f) of Article 46.

evidence.what: MA application: written confirmation (QP Declaration)

points.question: Does the finished product manufacturer use only active substances made under GMP and distributed under GDP?
points.verify: Verify that the finished product manufacturer uses only active substances which have been manufactured in accordance with good manufacturing practice for active substances and distributed in accordance with good distribution practices for active substances.

evidence.what: records showing GMP manufacture and GDP distribution of active substances used

points.question: Does the written confirmation give the audit date and declare that the audit result confirms GMP compliance?
points.verify: Verify that the written confirmation submitted by the applicant contains a reference to the date of the audit and a declaration that the outcome of the audit confirms that the manufacturing complies with the principles and guidelines of good manufacturing practice.

evidence.what: written confirmation (QP Declaration) submitted by the applicant

points.question: Did the MA applicant confirm the audits were done before submitting and is it satisfied with the active substance maker's GMP status?
points.verify: Verify that the MA applicant has confirmed that such audits have been carried out prior to the submission of the MA application, and is satisfied with the GMP compliance status of the manufacturer of the active substance, as determined by the holder of the medicinal product manufacturing authorisation.

evidence.what: applicant's confirmation and audit dates against the submission date
records showing the applicant is satisfied with the GMP compliance status

points.question: Is the applicant's confirmation given as a QP Declaration (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the confirmation is made in the form of a QP Declaration (recommended).

evidence.what: QP Declaration

points.question: For veterinary products, do the manufacturing processes of the active substance and the finished product follow GMP?
points.verify: Verify that, in relation to medicinal products for veterinary use, the manufacturing processes for the active substance(s) and finished product comply with Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP).

evidence.what: records showing GMP compliance of the active substance and finished product manufacturing processes

points.question: For veterinary products, are only GMP-made and GDP-distributed active substances used as starting materials?
points.verify: Verify that the holder of a manufacturing authorisation uses as starting materials only active substances which have been manufactured in accordance with good manufacturing practice for active substances and distributed in accordance with good distribution practice for active substances.

evidence.what: records showing GMP manufacture and GDP distribution of active substances used as starting materials

points.question: For veterinary products, is there an audit-based declaration from the QP of the manufacturing authorisation holder?
points.verify: Verify that a declaration(s) from the Qualified Person of the manufacturing authorisation holder is provided, and that for medicinal products for veterinary use a QP Declaration based on an audit is also in place.

evidence.what: QP declaration(s) for the veterinary product

points.question: After authorisation, does the MAH keep confirming the active substance maker's GMP status to the authority?
points.verify: Verify that the responsibility to confirm to the competent authority the GMP status of the active substance manufacturer continues into the post-authorisation phase of the medicinal product, and that the MAH bears this responsibility.

evidence.what: post-authorisation confirmations sent by the MAH to the competent authority

points.question: Does the MAH make sure the authority receives the written GMP confirmation for the active substance manufacturer?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH ensures that a written confirmation of compliance of the manufacturer of the active substance with GMP is provided to the competent authority.

evidence.what: written confirmation provided to the competent authority

points.question: Can the audit reports be produced quickly and given to the authorities on request (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the audit reports are readily available and are shared with the authorities, if requested (recommended).

evidence.what: audit reports on file
records of reports shared with authorities on request

points.question: Is the active substance maker's GMP status confirmed by the finished product maker from its audits and passed to the MAH?
points.verify: Verify that the GMP compliance status of the active substance manufacturer is confirmed by the manufacturer of the finished product and transmitted to the MAH, and that such confirmations (declarations) are based on audits carried out by, or on behalf of, the manufacturer of the finished product, as required by Article 46(f) of Directive 2001/83/EC and Article 93 (l) of Regulation 2019/6.

evidence.what: confirmations (declarations) transmitted to the MAH
audit reports behind the confirmations

points.question: Do records show audits, based on a risk assessment, of the firms from which active substances are obtained?
points.verify: Verify that, as Article 93 (l) requires, the holder of a MA performs audits based on a risk assessment of the manufacturers, distributors and importers from whom the holder of a manufacturing authorisation obtains active substances.

evidence.what: risk assessment of the active substance manufacturers, distributors and importers
audit reports

points.question: Are GMP audits of the manufacturer carried out again?
points.verify: Verify that GMP audits of the manufacturer are again carried out, such audits being those referred to in the guidelines concerning MA variations (Ref. EC Guidelines 2013/C 223/01 and Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/17 of 8 January 2021).

evidence.what: GMP audit reports of the manufacturer

points.question: When the audit date of the active substance manufacturer changes, does the MAH notify it by a Type 1A variation or another accepted route?
points.verify: Verify that, as the section dealing with Administrative Changes of the aforementioned guidelines places this responsibility on the MAH, the MAH submits a Type 1A variation notification in relation to changes in the date of the audit to verify GMP compliance of the manufacturer of the active substance; a variation application is not needed when the information has been otherwise transmitted to the authorities (e.g. through a QP declaration).

evidence.what: Type 1A variation notifications or other transmission (e.g. QP declaration) to the authorities
audit dates

points.question: Does the MAH supply the finished product maker's written confirmation that the active substance maker's GMP compliance was verified?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH provides a written confirmation from the manufacturer of the finished product stating verification of compliance of the manufacturer of the active substance with principles and guidelines of good manufacturing practices (Ref. Administrative Change A.8).

evidence.what: written confirmation from the finished product manufacturer

points.question: Are the GMP confirmations backed by audits of each site at regular intervals, normally within three years, with a reason given when that period is passed (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that such confirmations of compliance are based on audits, that audits of each site for GMP compliance are undertaken at regular intervals, normally within three years, and that justification is provided if the date since the last audit exceeds this period (recommended).

evidence.what: audit reports and audit dates for each site
justification where the period is exceeded

points.question: Is there a written contract or technical agreement that sets out what the manufacturer and the sponsor each do (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the responsibilities of the manufacturer and sponsor are appropriately defined, agreed and controlled in a written contract or technical agreement, as mentioned in recital 4 to the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 2017/1569, and that the agreement clearly establishes the duties of each party, taking into account the guidance in EudraLex, Volume 4, Part I, Chapter 7, as applicable (recommended).

evidence.what: written contract or technical agreement between manufacturer and sponsor

points.question: Does the technical agreement deal with the sourcing of authorised products for the trial and with recall arrangements (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where applicable, the technical agreement covers ensuring that any authorised products used in the clinical trial are sourced from an authorized vendor and that arrangements for recall are in place (recommended).

evidence.what: contract or technical agreement

points.question: Does the technical agreement deal with giving the QP the latest information for batch certification (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where applicable, the technical agreement covers ensuring that the most up to date information is provided to the QP for consideration during the batch certification process in accordance with the documents set out in the clinical trial applications authorised by EU member states (recommended).

evidence.what: contract or technical agreement

points.question: Does the technical agreement deal with how planned changes to manufacturing and control methods are passed between manufacturer and sponsor (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where applicable, the technical agreement covers ensuring that any proposed revision of manufacturing and control methods is appropriately communicated between the manufacturer and the sponsor, as this may need submission of a substantial modification to the clinical trial application (recommended).

evidence.what: contract or technical agreement

points.question: Does the technical agreement set out the un-blinding arrangements and who is responsible for what (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where applicable, the technical agreement covers ensuring that un-blinding arrangements and the respective responsibilities of each party are appropriately defined (recommended).

evidence.what: contract or technical agreement

points.question: Does the technical agreement stop agreed responsibilities being passed to a third party without the contract giver's prior evaluation and approval (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where applicable, the technical agreement covers ensuring that any agreed responsibilities are not subcontracted to a third party without prior evaluation and approval from the contract giver (recommended).

evidence.what: contract or technical agreement

points.question: Does the technical agreement keep trial master file documents available to the sponsor after the retention periods end (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where applicable, the technical agreement covers ensuring that the documentation needed in the clinical trial master file (e.g. IMP batch certification by the QP (https://ec.europa.eu/health/sites/default/files/files/eudralex/vol-4/template_imp_batch_certification.docx), documentation related to assembly and packaging of IMPs, Certificate of Analysis) remains available to the sponsor, in accordance with 58 of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014, after the retention periods as defined in Article 8 of the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/1569 on GMP for IMPs expire (recommended).

evidence.what: contract or technical agreement

points.question: Does the technical agreement deal with where and under what conditions reference and retention samples are kept (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where applicable, the technical agreement covers ensuring that the storage condition and location of reference and retention samples is defined and documented (recommended).

evidence.what: contract or technical agreement

points.question: Where the sponsor uses a chain of contracted manufacturers, does the technical agreement state each manufacturer's exact role (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where applicable, where the sponsor is not the IMP manufacturer and relies on a chain of contracted manufacturers, the technical agreement specifies the exact role of each manufacturer (e.g. specific tasks and GMP and GDP related responsibilities) in the chain of manufacturers (recommended).

evidence.what: contracts or technical agreements with the manufacturers in the chain

points.question: Does the technical agreement say who handles deviations that happen while IMPs are shipped to trial sites (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where applicable, the technical agreement defines responsibilities for the handling of deviations during shipment to clinical trial sites (recommended).

evidence.what: contract or technical agreement

points.question: Does the technical agreement set out what applies when IMPs are exceptionally moved between trial sites (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where applicable, the technical agreement defines requirements for the exceptional process of transferring IMPs from one clinical trial site to another (recommended).

evidence.what: contract or technical agreement

points.question: Are starting and raw materials checked against their requirements before they enter the process (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, prior to introduction in the manufacturing process, the conformity of the starting and raw materials to the relevant requirements is checked (recommended).

evidence.what: records of conformity checks before use in manufacturing

points.question: Is special care taken to avoid contamination of starting and raw materials and to minimise their variability as much as possible (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that particular attention is paid to avoiding contamination and to minimising as much as possible the variability of the starting and raw materials (recommended).

evidence.what: procedures or records showing measures against contamination and variability of starting and raw materials
handling of starting and raw materials

points.question: Do the raw materials for ATMP manufacture take the Ph. Eur chapter on biological-origin raw materials into account as far as possible (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, as far as possible, raw materials used in the manufacturing of ATMPs take into consideration the Ph. Eur 5.2.12 general chapter on raw materials of biological origin for the production of cell based and gene therapy medicinal products (recommended).

evidence.what: raw material specifications or records showing consideration of Ph. Eur 5.2.12

points.question: Are pharmaceutical grade raw materials used (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that raw materials are of pharmaceutical grade; it is acknowledged that, in some cases, only materials of research grade are available (recommended).

evidence.what: raw material specifications showing grade
records showing the grade of raw materials received

points.question: Where research grade materials are used, are their risks understood and their fitness for use ensured (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the risks of using research grade materials are understood (including the risks to the continuity of supply when larger amounts of product are manufactured), and that the suitability of such raw materials for the intended use is ensured, including, where appropriate, by means of testing (e.g. functional test, safety test) (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing the risks of research grade materials are understood
records showing suitability for intended use, including testing where appropriate

points.question: Are raw material specifications properly set, complete for critical materials and in line with the authorisation (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that specifications for raw materials are set as explained in Section 6.2; that, in the case of critical raw materials, the specifications include quality requirements to ensure suitability for the intended use, as well as the acceptance criteria; and that the specifications set are in compliance with the terms of the marketing authorisation or clinical trial authorisation (recommended).

evidence.what: raw material specifications
marketing authorisation or clinical trial authorisation terms

points.question: Have the specifications for critical raw materials been agreed with suppliers, and do they cover the expected aspects (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, for authorised ATMPs, the quality requirements for critical raw materials are agreed with the supplier(s) (agreed specifications); that, for investigational ATMPs, the technical specifications for the critical raw materials are agreed with the suppliers whenever possible; and that the agreed specifications cover aspects of the production, testing and control, and other aspects of handling and distribution as appropriate (recommended).

evidence.what: specifications agreed with the supplier(s)

points.question: Is there a documented, risk-based decision on which raw materials are critical (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the assessment whether a specific raw material is critical is done by the manufacturer (or, as appropriate, the sponsor or marketing authorisation holder) having regard to the specific risks, and that the decisions taken are documented (recommended).

evidence.what: documented criticality assessment and decisions for raw materials

points.question: Does the ATMP manufacturer check supplier materials against the agreed specifications, with oversight matched to risk (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the ATMP manufacturer verifies compliance of the supplier's materials with the agreed specifications, and that the level of supervision and further testing by the ATMP manufacturer is proportionate to the risks posed by the individual materials (recommended).

evidence.what: records of verification of supplier materials against agreed specifications
procedure or records showing level of supervision and testing per material risk

points.question: Where the supplier's certificate of analysis is relied on, are all risks understood and controlled (recommended)?
points.verify: Where reliance is placed on the certificate of analysis of the supplier, verify that all the risks are duly understood and measures are put in place to eliminate the risks or mitigate them to an acceptable level (e.g. qualification of suppliers) (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing the risks are understood and the measures in place

points.question: Where they are available, are authorised medicinal products used as raw materials (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where available, authorised medicinal products are used (their use is encouraged) (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing raw materials used and their authorisation status

points.question: Has the contamination risk of biological-origin raw materials along the supply chain been assessed?
points.verify: Verify that the risk of contamination of raw materials of biological origin during their passage along the supply chain is assessed, with particular emphasis on viral and microbial safety and Transmissible Spongiform Encephalopathy (TSE).

evidence.what: contamination risk assessment for raw materials of biological origin

points.question: Where a raw material carries a possible mycoplasma risk, is it filtered before use unless the supplier certified it mycoplasma free (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where there is a potential mycoplasma contamination risk associated with a raw material, the ATMP manufacturer filters the material prior to use (0.1 μm filter), unless the supplier of the raw material has certified that the raw material has been tested and is mycoplasma free (recommended).

evidence.what: records of filtration of the raw material prior to use
supplier certification that the material was tested and is mycoplasma free

points.question: Do supplier records show that human tissues and cells used as starting materials were donated, procured and tested under the applicable Directive (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the donation, procurement and testing of human tissues and cells used as starting materials are in accordance with Directive 2004/23/EC; for blood-derived cells, compliance with Directive 2002/98/EC regarding donation, procurement and testing is likewise acceptable (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing donation, procurement and testing compliance of human tissues and cells

points.question: Has the starting material supplier's accreditation, designation, authorisation or licence been checked (recommended)?

evidence.what: personnel training and qualification records

points.question: Do the finished product QC results meet the specification in the marketing authorisation or the authorised real time release programme?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that finished product quality control (QC) test data complies with the Finished Product Specification described in the MA, or where authorised, the Real Time Release Testing programme.

evidence.what: finished product QC test data
Finished Product Specification in the MA
Real Time Release Testing programme, where authorised

points.question: Have post-marketing commitments to regulators on manufacture or testing been dealt with?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that any regulatory post-marketing commitments relating to manufacture or testing of the product have been addressed.

evidence.what: records showing post-marketing commitments addressed

points.question: Do the on-going stability results still back certification?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that on-going stability data continues to support certification.

evidence.what: on-going stability data

points.question: Has the effect of every manufacturing or testing change been assessed and any extra checks and tests finished?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that the impact of any change to product manufacturing or testing has been evaluated and any additional checks and tests are complete.

evidence.what: change impact evaluations
results of additional checks and tests

points.question: Are all investigations on the batch, OOS and OOT included, far enough along to support certification?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that all investigations pertaining to the batch being certified (including out of specification and out of trend investigations) have been completed to a sufficient level to support certification.

evidence.what: investigation records for the batch

points.question: Has it been checked that open complaints, investigations or recalls do not stop this batch from being certified?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that any on-going complaints, investigations or recalls do not negate the conditions for certification of the batch in question.

evidence.what: on-going complaint, investigation and recall records
QP

points.question: Are the technical agreements that are needed in place?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that the required technical agreements are in place.

evidence.what: technical agreements

points.question: Is the self-inspection programme running and up to date?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that the self-inspection programme is active and current.

evidence.what: self-inspection programme
self-inspection records

points.question: Are suitable distribution and shipment arrangements in place?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that the appropriate arrangements for distribution and shipment are in place.

evidence.what: distribution and shipment arrangements

points.question: For human medicines meant for the Union market, are the safety features on the packaging where appropriate?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that, in the case of medicinal products for human use intended to be placed on the market in the Union, the safety features referred to in Article 54(o) of Directive 2001/83/EC, as amended, have been affixed to the packaging, where appropriate.

evidence.what: packaging records showing safety features
safety features on packs

points.question: For parallel import or parallel distribution, is there authority approval for repackaging of an already released batch?
points.verify: Verify that, in the case of parallel importation and parallel distribution, any repackaging operation carried out on a batch which has already been released is approved by the competent authority of the intended market.

evidence.what: competent authority approval for repackaging

points.question: Before certifying a repacked batch, does the QP confirm the parallel importation and parallel distribution rules are met (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, prior to certification of a repacked batch, the QP confirms compliance with national requirements for parallel importation and EU rules for parallel distribution (recommended).

evidence.what: QP confirmation for the repacked batch

points.question: Does the QP named in the marketing authorisation of the repackaged product certify how the repackaging was done?
points.verify: Verify that the QP of the MIA holder, who is named responsible for the certification of the batch in the MA of the repackaged finished product, certifies that the repackaging has been performed in accordance with the relevant authorisation pertaining to the repackaged product and GMP.

evidence.what: certification of the repackaged batch
MA of the repackaged finished product

points.question: Does the QP enter each certification in a register or similar document kept for this?
points.verify: Verify that the certification of a medicinal product is recorded by the QP in a register or equivalent document provided for that purpose.

evidence.what: certification register or equivalent document

points.question: Does the certification record show that each production batch meets the Directive provisions (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the record shows that each production batch satisfies the provisions of Article 51 of Directive 2001/83/EC, as amended, or Article 55 of Directive 2001/82/EC (recommended).

evidence.what: certification register or equivalent document

points.question: Is the certification record kept current and held ready for the authority for the set period, five years at least?
points.verify: Verify that the record is kept up to date as operations are carried out and remains at the disposal of the agents of the competent authority for the period specified in the provisions of the Member State concerned and in any event for at least five years.

evidence.what: certification register or equivalent document

points.question: Is the control report or other proof of release provided for a batch going to another Member State (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the control report referred to in Article 51 of Directive 2001/83/EC, as amended, or Article 55 of Directive 2001/82/EC or another proof for release to the market in question, based on an equivalent system, is made available for the batch in order to be exempted from further controls when entering another Member State (recommended).

evidence.what: control report or other proof of release for the batch

points.question: Where a QP confirms or certifies a batch after an unexpected deviation, were all registered specifications met (recommended)?
points.verify: Where a QP confirms compliance or certifies a batch where an unexpected deviation concerning the manufacturing process and/or the analytical control methods from details contained within the MA and/or GMP has occurred, verify that registered specifications for active substances, excipients, packaging materials and medicinal products are met (recommended).

evidence.what: deviation record for the batch
test results against registered specifications

points.question: Do records show a thorough investigation of the deviation and correction of its root cause (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the deviation is thoroughly investigated and the root cause corrected (recommended).

evidence.what: deviation investigation records
records showing the root cause corrected

points.question: Is the effect of the deviation assessed through a quality risk management process (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the impact of the deviation is assessed in accordance with a quality risk management process using an appropriate approach such as described in Part III of the GMP Guide (recommended).

evidence.what: risk assessment of the deviation

points.question: Does the risk assessment of the deviation cover batch impact, stability follow-up and, for biologicals, unexpected effects (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the quality risk management process includes: evaluation of the potential impact of the deviation on quality, safety or efficacy of the batch(es) concerned and conclusion that the impact is negligible; consideration of the need to include the affected batch(es) in the ongoing stability programme; and, in the case of biological medicinal products, consideration that any deviations from the approved process can have an unexpected impact on safety and efficacy (recommended).

evidence.what: risk assessment of the deviation

points.question: Does the certifying QP know of and weigh deviations that could affect GMP or marketing authorisation compliance, also when several QPs share the work (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, taking account that responsibilities may be shared between more than one QPs involved in the manufacture and control of a batch, the QP performing certification of a batch of medicinal product is aware of and takes into consideration any deviations which have the potential to impact compliance with GMP and/or compliance with the MA (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing deviations considered by the certifying QP
certifying QP

points.question: Where dealing with an unexpected deviation calls for a variation to the marketing authorisation to keep making the product, has the variation been submitted (recommended)?
points.verify: Where the investigation of an unexpected deviation and the correction of its root cause make a variation to the MA necessary for the continued manufacture of the product, verify that the variation is submitted (recommended).

evidence.what: deviation records showing whether a variation to the MA is needed
variation submission to the MA

points.question: Do records show that batches go out for sale or supply only once a QP has certified them (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that batches of medicinal products are only released for sale or supply to the market after certification by a QP as described above (recommended).

evidence.what: batch certification records
batch release records

points.question: Does an uncertified batch stay at the manufacturing site or move only under quarantine to an authority-approved site (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, until a batch is certified, it remains at the site of manufacture or is shipped under quarantine to another site which has been approved for that purpose by the relevant Competent Authority (recommended).

evidence.what: shipment records of uncertified batches
Competent Authority approval of the receiving site
uncertified batches held at the site

points.question: Are there safeguards that stop uncertified batches from reaching saleable stock (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that safeguards to ensure that uncertified batches are not transferred to saleable stock are in place; they may be physical in nature, e.g. the use of segregation and labelling, or electronic in nature, e.g. the use of validated computerised systems (recommended).

evidence.what: safeguards on uncertified batches
procedure describing the safeguards

points.question: Do the safeguards against early release stay in force when uncertified batches move between authorised sites (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, when uncertified batches are moved from one authorised site to another, the safeguards to prevent premature release remain (recommended).

evidence.what: transfer records of uncertified batches
safeguards on transferred batches

points.question: Does a technical agreement set out how the stock site is told about QP certification (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the steps necessary to notify QP certification to the site where the transfer to saleable stock is to take place are defined within a technical agreement (recommended).

evidence.what: technical agreement

points.question: Is the QP's notice of certification to the site formal, clear and handled under the documentation chapter (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that such notification by a QP to the site is formal and unambiguous and is subject to the requirements of Chapter 4 of EudraLex, Volume 4, Part I (recommended).

evidence.what: QP notifications of certification

points.question: Does the confirmation of partial manufacturing identify the manufacturer, the product and stage, the batch and the site?
points.verify: Verify that the confirmation of partial manufacturing carries the letter head of the manufacturer who carried out the manufacturing activity and gives the name of the product and a description of the manufacturing stage (e.g. paracetamol 500 mg tablets, primary packaging into blister packs), the batch number, and the name and address of the site carrying out the partial manufacturing.

evidence.what: confirmations of partial manufacturing

points.question: Does the confirmation of partial manufacturing refer to the Technical Quality Agreement?
points.verify: Verify that the confirmation of partial manufacturing contains a reference to the Technical Quality Agreement (in accordance with Chapter 7 of the Guide).

evidence.what: confirmations of partial manufacturing

points.question: Does the confirmation of partial manufacturing contain the full confirmation statement on GMP and agreement compliance?
points.verify: Verify that the confirmation of partial manufacturing contains a confirmation statement saying that the manufacturing stages referred to in the Technical Quality Agreement have been carried out in full compliance with the GMP requirements of the EU and the terms described in the Agreement for ensuring compliance with the requirements of the Marketing Authorisation(s) as provided by the Contract Giver/manufacturer certifying and releasing the batch.

evidence.what: confirmations of partial manufacturing

points.question: Is the confirmation of partial manufacturing named, signed and dated by the Qualified Person?
points.verify: Verify that the confirmation of partial manufacturing shows the name of the Qualified Person confirming the partial manufacturing, the signature of the Qualified Person confirming the partial manufacturing, and the date of signature.

evidence.what: confirmations of partial manufacturing

points.question: Does the batch certificate identify the releasing manufacturer, the product, the batch and the destination?
points.verify: Verify that the batch certificate carries the letter head of the batch certifying and releasing manufacturer and gives the name, strength/potency, dosage form and package size (identical to the text on the finished product package), the batch number of the finished product, and the name of the destination country/countries of the batch, at least when within the EU.

evidence.what: batch certificates
text on the finished product package

points.question: Does the batch certificate contain the full certification statement on GMP and marketing authorisation compliance?
points.verify: Verify that the batch certificate contains a certification statement saying that all the manufacturing stages of this batch of finished product have been carried out in full compliance with the GMP requirements of the EU and, when within the EU, with the requirements of the Marketing Authorisation(s) of the destination country/countries.

evidence.what: batch certificates

points.question: Is the batch certificate named, signed and dated by the Qualified Person?
points.verify: Verify that the batch certificate shows the name of the Qualified Person certifying the batch, the signature of the Qualified Person certifying the batch, and the date of signature.

evidence.what: batch certificates

points.question: Where process information is used instead of end-product testing for batch release, is this authorised and based on product and process knowledge (recommended)?
points.verify: Where information collected during the manufacturing process is used instead of end-product testing for batch release, verify that this is in specific circumstances, authorised, and based on product knowledge and process understanding (recommended).

evidence.what: authorisation for this form of batch release
batch release records

points.question: Are the separate activities needed for this form of batch release built into the quality system (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that any separate activities needed for this form of batch release are integrated into the Pharmaceutical Quality System (PQS) (recommended).

evidence.what: PQS documents covering this form of batch release

points.question: Do records show contact with the regulatory authorities before and during the assessment that leads to RTRT approval?
points.verify: Verify that there was interaction with all relevant regulatory authorities prior and during the assessment process preceding regulatory approval.

evidence.what: records of interaction with regulatory authorities

points.question: Does the RTRT design show that real time measurement and control predict the finished product attributes accurately (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, when designing the RTRT strategy, the following minimum criterion is established and met: real time measurement and control of relevant in-process material attributes and process parameters are accurate predictors of the corresponding finished product attributes (recommended).

evidence.what: RTRT strategy
data showing the prediction of finished product attributes

points.question: Is the combination of attributes and controls that replaces finished product attributes backed by scientific evidence (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, when designing the RTRT strategy, the following minimum criterion is established and met: the valid combination of relevant assessed material attributes and process controls to replace finished product attributes is established with scientific evidence based on material, product and process knowledge (recommended).

evidence.what: RTRT strategy
scientific evidence for the combination

points.question: Do the process measurements and other in-process test data give a robust basis for RTRT and batch release (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, when designing the RTRT strategy, the following minimum criterion is established and met: the combined process measurements (process parameters and material attributes) and any other test data generated during the manufacturing process provide a robust foundation for RTRT and the batch release decision (recommended).

evidence.what: RTRT strategy
process measurements and test data from manufacturing

points.question: Is the RTRT strategy built into the quality system and controlled through it (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the RTRT strategy is integrated and controlled through the PQS (recommended).

evidence.what: PQS documents covering the RTRT strategy

points.question: Does the RTRT strategy in the quality system cover risk management, change control and the control strategy (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the RTRT strategy in the PQS includes or references information at least of: quality risk management, including a full process related risk assessment, in accordance with the principles described in EudraLex, Volume 4, Part I Chapter 1 and Part II Chapter 2; the change control program; and the control strategy (recommended).

evidence.what: PQS documents covering the RTRT strategy

points.question: Does the RTRT strategy in the quality system cover training, qualification and validation, and deviations/CAPA (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the RTRT strategy in the PQS includes or references information at least of: the specific personnel training program; the qualification and validation policy; and the deviation/CAPA system (recommended).

evidence.what: PQS documents covering the RTRT strategy

points.question: Does the RTRT strategy in the quality system cover sensor or equipment failure and periodic review of the RTRT plan (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the RTRT strategy in the PQS includes or references information at least of: a contingency procedure in case of a process sensor/equipment failure; and a periodic review/assessment program to measure the effectiveness of the RTRT plan for continued assurance of product quality (recommended).

evidence.what: PQS documents covering the RTRT strategy

points.question: Do change records show a risk and reproducibility assessment, a risk-based justification and full documentation (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that any change that could potentially impact product manufacturing and testing, or the validated status of facilities, systems, equipment, analytical methods or processes, is assessed for risk to product quality and impact on reproducibility of the manufacturing process (recommended). Verify that any change is justified by the sound application of quality risk management principles, and fully documented (recommended).

evidence.what: change records with assessments and justifications

points.question: Is each change evaluated after it is implemented to show no harm to product quality (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, after change implementation, an evaluation is undertaken to demonstrate that there are no unintended or deleterious impact on product quality (recommended).

evidence.what: evaluations done after change implementation

points.question: Is the control strategy designed to keep the process in control and not only to monitor it (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the control strategy is designed not only to monitor the process, but also to maintain a state of control and ensure that a product of the required quality will be consistently produced (recommended).

evidence.what: control strategy

points.question: Does the control strategy explain and justify what is routinely monitored, and describe sampling and acceptance/rejection criteria (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the control strategy describes and justifies the selected in-process controls, material attributes and process parameters which require to be routinely monitored and is based on product, formulation and process understanding (recommended). Verify that the control strategy also describes the sampling plan and acceptance/rejection criteria (recommended).

evidence.what: control strategy

points.question: Where the control strategy changes during the product lifecycle, are quality risk management and knowledge management used (recommended)?
points.verify: Where the control strategy changes throughout the lifecycle of the product, verify that a quality risk management approach and knowledge management are used (recommended).

evidence.what: records of changes to the control strategy

points.question: Do training records show specific RTRT training for personnel (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that personnel are given specific training on RTRT technologies, principles and procedures (recommended).

evidence.what: RTRT training records

points.question: Can key personnel show enough experience and product and process knowledge (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that key personnel demonstrate adequate experience, product and process knowledge and understanding (recommended).

evidence.what: key personnel
records of experience of key personnel

points.question: Did a team from several functions and disciplines give input to the RTRT implementation (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that RTRT implementation had input from a cross-functional/multi-disciplinary team with relevant experience on specific topics, such as engineering, analytics, chemometric modeling or statistics (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing the team's input to RTRT implementation

points.question: Is particular attention given to in-line and on-line analytical methods with the probe inside the equipment (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that particular attention is focused on the qualification, validation and management of in-line and on-line analytical methods, where the sampling probe is placed within the manufacturing equipment (recommended).

evidence.what: qualification and validation records of in-line and on-line methods
procedure for managing in-line and on-line methods

points.question: Do records show full investigation of deviations and process failures and follow-up of adverse trends (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that any deviation or process failure is thoroughly investigated and any adverse trending indicating a change in the state of control is followed up appropriately (recommended).

evidence.what: deviation and process failure investigations
trend data and follow-up records

points.question: Is learning from product data over the life cycle built into the quality system (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that continuous learning through data collection and analysis over the life cycle of a product is part of the PQS (recommended).

evidence.what: PQS documents on data collection and analysis
data collection and analysis records

points.question: Does the manufacturer assess observed data trends scientifically for chances to improve quality or consistency (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the manufacturer scientifically evaluates the data, in consultation if appropriate with the regulatory authorities, to determine how or if such data trends indicate opportunities to improve quality and/or consistency (recommended).

evidence.what: scientific evaluations of data trends

points.question: Once RTRT is approved, is it the routine way batches are released (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, when RTRT has been approved, this approach is routinely used for batch release (recommended).

evidence.what: batch release records

points.question: When RTRT results fail or trend toward failure, does the site avoid switching to end-product testing?
points.verify: Verify that, in the event that the results from RTRT fail or are trending toward failure, the RTRT approach is not substituted by end-product testing.

evidence.what: batch release records of batches with failing or adverse-trending RTRT results

points.question: Are RTRT failures investigated and taken into account when deciding batch release?
points.verify: Verify that any failure is thoroughly investigated and considered in the batch release decision depending on the results of these investigations (recommended), and that this complies with the content of the marketing authorisation and GMP requirements.

evidence.what: failure investigation records
batch release decisions for the affected batches

points.question: Do records show that trends are followed up (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that trends are followed up appropriately (recommended).

evidence.what: trend data and follow-up records

points.question: Do Certificates of Analysis still list attributes controlled indirectly by RTRT, with the set wording and footnote (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that attributes (e.g. uniformity of content) that are indirectly controlled by approved RTRT still appear in the Certificate of Analysis for batches (recommended). Verify that the approved method for end-product testing is mentioned and the results are given as “Complies if tested” with a footnote: “Controlled by approved Real Time Release Testing” (recommended).

evidence.what: Certificates of Analysis of batches

points.question: Does the certifying QP make sure the safety features are on the packaging where they are needed?
points.verify: Verify that the QP certifying the batch is responsible for ensuring that, where required, the safety features have been affixed to the packaging.

evidence.what: procedure or QP responsibilities for batch certification
batch certification records showing safety features were ensured

points.question: Does the certifying QP make sure reference and retention samples have been taken?
points.verify: Verify that the certifying QP is also responsible for ensuring that reference and retention samples have been taken in accordance with the requirements in Annex 19 of the EU GMP Guide and applicable detailed guidelines for GMP for IMPs.

evidence.what: procedure or QP responsibilities for batch certification
batch certification records showing samples were ensured

points.question: Does the assessment of finished product look at all relevant factors and not only test results (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that finished product assessment embraces all relevant factors, including production conditions, results of in-process testing, a review of manufacturing (including packaging) documentation, compliance with Finished Product Specification and examination of the final finished pack (recommended).

evidence.what: procedure for finished product assessment
finished product assessment records

points.question: Are complaints and other reports of possibly defective products reviewed under written procedures and followed by corrective action?
points.verify: Verify that all complaints and other information concerning potentially defective products are carefully reviewed according to the written procedures and that corrective action is taken.

evidence.what: written procedures for complaint review
complaint review and corrective action records

points.question: Is there a named person in charge of complaints, with enough support staff?
points.verify: Verify that a person responsible for handling the complaints and deciding the measures to be taken is designated, together with sufficient supporting staff to assist him or her.

evidence.what: designation of the person responsible for complaints
complaint handling person and supporting staff

points.question: If the complaints person is not the authorised person, is the authorised person told of every complaint, investigation or recall?
points.verify: Verify that, if the person responsible for handling complaints is different from the authorised person, the authorised person is made aware of any complaint, investigation or recall.

evidence.what: records showing the authorised person was informed
authorised person

points.question: Do written procedures say what to do when a complaint about a possible product defect comes in, including thinking about a recall?
points.verify: Verify that there are written procedures describing the action to be taken, including the need to consider a recall, in the case of a complaint concerning a possible product defect.

evidence.what: written complaint procedures

points.question: Do complaint investigations pay special attention to finding out whether the complained product was really defective?
points.verify: Verify that special attention is given to establishing that the product that gave rise to a complaint was defective.

evidence.what: complaint investigation records

points.question: Are product defect complaints recorded with their original details, fully investigated, and reviewed with the QC head normally involved?
points.verify: Verify that any complaint concerning a product defect is recorded with all the original details and thoroughly investigated. Verify that the person responsible for Quality Control (QC) is normally involved in the review of such investigations.

evidence.what: complaint records and investigation reports
investigation review records showing QC involvement

points.question: When a batch has a known or suspected defect, does the site consider checking other batches and investigate batches holding reprocessed product from it?
points.verify: Verify that, if a product defect is identified or suspected in a batch, consideration is given as to whether other batches shall be checked in order to determine whether they are also affected. evidence.what: complaint and defect investigation records covering other batches

points.question: After a complaint is investigated and evaluated, is follow-up action taken where it is needed?
points.verify: Verify that, where necessary, appropriate follow-up action, possibly including product recall, is taken after investigation and evaluation of the complaint.

evidence.what: complaint records showing follow-up action

points.question: Are complaint decisions and measures written down and linked to the batch records?
points.verify: Verify that all decisions made and measures taken as a result of a complaint are recorded and referenced to the corresponding batch records.

evidence.what: complaint records
corresponding batch records

points.question: Are complaint records looked at regularly for specific or repeating problems?
points.verify: Verify that complaint records are regularly reviewed for any indication of specific or recurring problems that require attention and might justify the recall of marketed products.

evidence.what: records of regular review of complaint records

points.question: Are the licensing authorities told when the manufacturer is considering action over a serious quality problem?
points.verify: Verify that the licensing authorities are informed if the manufacturer is considering action following the faulty manufacture, product deterioration, a suspect product or any other serious quality problems with a product.

evidence.what: communications to the licensing authorities
records of serious quality problems and actions considered

points.question: Does the licensee run a pharmacovigilance system that sends adverse reaction reports to the licensing authorities?
points.verify: Verify that the licensee has a pharmacovigilance system in place for collecting, processing and forwarding the reports to the licensing authorities for information on the adverse drug reactions emerging from the use of drugs manufactured or marketed by the licensee.

evidence.what: pharmacovigilance system description
adverse drug reaction reports collected, processed and forwarded

points.question: Is a system in place to bring back defective or suspect products from the market?
points.verify: Verify that there is a system to recall from the market products known or suspected to be defective.

evidence.what: recall system description

points.question: Is the authorised person in charge of carrying out and coordinating recalls, with enough staff?
points.verify: Verify that the authorised person is responsible for the execution and coordination of recalls. Verify that he or she has sufficient staff to handle all aspects of the recalls with the appropriate degree of urgency.

evidence.what: assignment of recall responsibility and staff
authorised person

points.question: Are there written recall organisation procedures that are kept reviewed and up to date?
points.verify: Verify that there are established written procedures, which are regularly reviewed and updated, for the organisation of any recall activity.

evidence.what: written recall procedures and their review history

points.question: Can a recall be started at the level of the distribution chain that is needed?
points.verify: Verify that recall operations are capable of being initiated at the required level in the distribution chain.

evidence.what: recall procedures
recall records

points.question: Do the written procedures tell staff to keep recalled products in a secure segregated area?
points.verify: Verify that an instruction is included in the written procedures to store recalled products in a secure segregated area.

evidence.what: written recall procedures

points.question: Are the licensing authorities told whenever a recall for a defect or suspected defect is intended?
points.verify: Verify that the licensing authorities are informed of any intention to recall the product because it is, or is suspected of being, defective.

evidence.what: communications to the licensing authorities on recalls

points.question: Can the authorised person and the recall staff get the distribution records quickly, and do the records have enough customer details?
points.verify: Verify that the distribution records are readily available to the authorised person and contain sufficient information on wholesalers and directly supplied customers to permit an effective recall. evidence.what: distribution records
authorised person and persons designated for recall

points.question: Do recall records track progress, show what happened to the product, and end with a final report with reconciliation?
points.verify: Verify that the progress of the recall process is monitored and recorded and that the records include the disposition of the product. Verify that a final report is issued, including reconciliation between the delivered and recovered quantities of the products.

evidence.what: recall progress records
final recall reports

points.question: Does the designated person keep on record the final recall report with the quantity reconciliation?
points.verify: Verify that the designated person records a final report issued, including reconciliation between the delivered and the recovered quantities of the products.

evidence.what: final recall reports

points.question: Are the recall arrangements tested and their effectiveness evaluated from time to time?
points.verify: Verify that the effectiveness of the arrangements for recall is tested and evaluated from time to time.

evidence.what: records of testing and evaluation of recall arrangements

points.question: Is the recall system built to inform everyone in the supply chain down to retail quickly?
points.verify: Verify that a prompt and effective product recall system of defective products is devised for timely information of all concerned stockists, wholesalers, suppliers, up to the retail level within the shortest period.

evidence.what: recall system description
recall communication records

points.question: Is there an SOP for recalling the products the licensee has distributed?
points.verify: Verify that there is an established written procedure in the form of Standard Operating Procedure for effective recall of products distributed by the licensee.

evidence.what: recall Standard Operating Procedure

points.question: Can a recall be started so that it reaches every distribution channel level?
points.verify: Verify that recall operations are capable of being initiated, so as to effectively reach at the level of each distribution channel.

evidence.what: recall procedure
recall records

points.question: Are recalled products kept apart in a secured segregated area while the final decision on them is awaited?
points.verify: Verify that the recalled products are stored separately in a secured segregated area pending final decision on them.

evidence.what: area where recalled products are stored

points.question: Are recalled products marked and kept apart in a secure area, and is the decision on them taken quickly?
points.verify: Verify that recalled products are identified and stored separately in a secure area until a decision is taken, and that the decision is made as soon as possible.
