records of decisions on recalled products

points.question: Are market returns destroyed unless their quality is certain, and otherwise used only after a QC assessment under a written procedure?
points.verify: Verify that products returned from the market are destroyed unless it is certain that their quality is satisfactory. points.verify: Verify that, in cases where the true root cause(s) of the quality defect cannot be determined, consideration is given to identifying the most likely root cause(s) and to addressing those (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect investigation records

points.question: Are there written procedures for recalls and other risk-reducing actions, kept under regular review (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that there are established written procedures, regularly reviewed and updated when necessary, in order to undertake any recall activity or implement any other risk-reducing actions (recommended).

evidence.what: recall and risk-reducing action procedures
review and update history of these procedures

points.question: Is every retrieval of marketed product from distribution because of a quality defect handled as a recall (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, after a product has been placed on the market, any retrieval of it from the distribution network as a result of a quality defect is regarded and managed as a recall (recommended). This does not apply to the retrieval (or return) of samples of the product from the distribution network to facilitate an investigation into a quality defect issue/report (recommended).

evidence.what: recall procedure
records of product retrievals from the distribution network

points.question: Can a recall be started quickly and at any time (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that recall operations are capable of being initiated promptly and at any time (recommended).

evidence.what: recall procedure
staff responsible for recalls on how a recall is started

points.question: Can the people in charge of recalls readily get distribution records with enough customer details (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the batch/product distribution records are readily available to the persons responsible for recalls, and contain sufficient information on wholesalers and directly supplied customers (with addresses, phone and/or fax numbers inside and outside working hours, batches and amounts delivered), including those for exported products and medical samples (recommended).

evidence.what: batch/product distribution records
access of persons responsible for recalls to these records

points.question: For investigational medicinal products, are all trial sites and destination countries shown (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in the case of investigational medicinal products, all trial sites are identified and the countries of destination are indicated (recommended).

evidence.what: distribution records of investigational medicinal products

points.question: For an investigational product that also has a marketing authorisation, is the authorisation holder told of related quality defects (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in the case of an investigational medicinal product for which a marketing authorisation has been issued, the manufacturer of the investigational medicinal product, in cooperation with the sponsor, informs the marketing authorisation holder of any quality defect that could be related to the authorised medicinal product (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect communications to the marketing authorisation holder

points.question: Has the sponsor put in place a rapid unblinding procedure that reveals product identity only as far as needed (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the sponsor has implemented a procedure for the rapid unblinding of blinded products, where this is necessary for a prompt recall (recommended). Verify that the sponsor ensures that the procedure discloses the identity of the blinded product only in so far as is necessary (recommended).

evidence.what: sponsor's rapid unblinding procedure

points.question: Do recall records show that the depth of the recall in the distribution network was considered after consulting the authorities (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that consideration is given, following consultation with the concerned Competent Authorities, as to how far into the distribution network a recall action should extend, taking into account the potential risk to public or animal health and any impact that the proposed recall action may have (recommended).

evidence.what: recall decision records
consultation with the concerned Competent Authorities

points.question: Are the authorities told when no recall is proposed for a defective batch because it has expired (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the Competent Authorities are also informed in situations in which no recall action is being proposed for a defective batch because the batch has expired (such as with short shelf-life products) (recommended).

evidence.what: communications to the Competent Authorities on expired defective batches

points.question: Do records show that the authorities concerned were told before a planned recall (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that all concerned Competent Authorities are informed in advance in cases where products are intended to be recalled (recommended).

evidence.what: recall notifications to the concerned Competent Authorities

points.question: Where rapid actions for very serious issues come before notifying the authorities, was advance agreement tried wherever possible (recommended)?
points.verify: Where, for very serious issues (i.e. those with the potential to seriously impact upon patient or animal health), rapid risk-reducing actions (such as a product recall) are taken in advance of notifying the Competent Authorities, verify that, wherever possible, attempts are made to agree these in advance of their execution with the concerned Competent Authorities (recommended).

evidence.what: records of rapid risk-reducing actions
communications with the concerned Competent Authorities

points.question: Do recall records show a check for different effects in different markets and, if so, market-specific actions discussed with the authorities (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that it is also considered whether the proposed recall action may affect different markets in different ways, and, if this is the case, that appropriate market-specific risk-reducing actions are developed and discussed with the concerned competent authorities (recommended).

evidence.what: recall decision records
discussions with the concerned competent authorities

points.question: Before deciding on a recall or similar action, is the shortage risk weighed for a product with no authorised alternative (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, taking account of its therapeutic use, the risk of shortage of a medicinal product which has no authorised alternative is considered before deciding on a risk-reducing action such as a recall (recommended).

evidence.what: decision records for risk-reducing actions

points.question: Is any decision not to carry out a risk-reducing action agreed beforehand with the competent authority (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that any decisions not to execute a risk-reducing action which would otherwise be needed are agreed with the competent authority in advance (recommended).

evidence.what: competent authority agreement on file
decision records for risk-reducing actions

points.question: Are recalled products marked and kept apart in a secure area until their fate is decided (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that recalled products are identified and stored separately in a secure area while awaiting a decision on their fate (recommended).

evidence.what: storage area for recalled products
records of recalled product storage

points.question: Is there a formal, written disposition for every recalled batch (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that a formal disposition of all recalled batches is made and documented (recommended).

evidence.what: disposition records of recalled batches

points.question: Is the reason for any rework of recalled products written down and discussed with the authority (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the rationale for any decision to rework recalled products is documented and discussed with the relevant competent authority (recommended).

evidence.what: documented rationale for rework of recalled products
discussion with the relevant competent authority

points.question: For reworked batches that may go back on the market, is the remaining shelf-life taken into account (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the extent of shelf-life remaining for any reworked batches that are being considered for placement onto the market is also considered (recommended).

evidence.what: decision records for reworked recalled batches

points.question: Is each recall tracked in writing to closure, ending with a final report that reconciles quantities (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the progress of the recall process is recorded until closure and a final report is issued, including a reconciliation between the delivered and recovered quantities of the concerned products/batches (recommended).

evidence.what: recall progress records
final recall reports with reconciliation

points.question: Are the recall arrangements evaluated from time to time, for office and out-of-office hours, with the evaluation written down and justified (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the effectiveness of the arrangements in place for recalls is periodically evaluated to confirm that they remain robust and fit for use; that such evaluations extend to both within office-hour situations and out-of-office hour situations and that, when performing them, consideration is given as to whether mock-recall actions should be performed; and that this evaluation is documented and justified (recommended).

evidence.what: documented evaluations of recall arrangements

points.question: Are risk-reducing actions other than recalls looked at case by case and discussed with the authorities (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that other potential risk-reducing actions are considered on a case-by-case basis and discussed with the concerned competent authorities (recommended).

evidence.what: decision records for risk-reducing actions
discussions with the concerned competent authorities

points.question: Can a recall be started before the cause and full size of the defect are known, when health protection needs it (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in certain cases where this is needed to protect public or animal health, recall operations can be initiated prior to establishing the root cause(s) and full extent of the quality defect (recommended).

evidence.what: recall procedure
records of recall operations

points.question: In a serious or possibly life-threatening case, do records show that the authorities were told and asked for advice (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in the event of a serious or potentially life-threatening situation, local, national, and/or international authorities are informed and their advice is sought (recommended).

evidence.what: records of informing authorities and seeking their advice
procedure for serious or potentially life-threatening situations

points.question: Where complaints, defects and recalls are managed centrally, are each party's roles written down and are delays avoided (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where the management of complaints, quality defects and recalls is performed centrally, the relative roles and responsibilities of the concerned parties are documented and that such central management does not result in delays in the investigation and management of the issue (recommended).

evidence.what: documented roles and responsibilities of the concerned parties
complaint, quality defect and recall records showing timelines

points.question: Is there evidence that the MAH is satisfied with the centralised way quality defects are handled, including the contact persons (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH is satisfied with the centralised arrangements that are in place for handling quality defects, such as within corporate quality groups or at manufacturing site(s), including the arrangements regarding the contact persons who may communicate quality defect issues to the competent authorities (and the EMA in the case of products authorised via the Centralised Procedure) (recommended).

evidence.what: centralised quality defect handling arrangements
records showing the MAH is satisfied with these arrangements

points.question: Does the applicant/MAH have a named contact person for product defects and recalls, given in the MA application form (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the applicant/MAH has, as expected, a dedicated responsible person to serve as a contact person for product defects and recalls in the post-authorisation phase, and that the applicant/MAH has, as expected, provided information on its contact person in the MA-application form (Ref. MA Application Form in Notice to Applicants Volume 2B, Article 6 of Regulation 726/2004, Annex I to Directive 2001/83/EC, Volume 6B of the Notice to Applicants, and Annex II of Regulation 6/2019) (recommended).

evidence.what: designation of the contact person for product defects and recalls
MA-application form

points.question: Have the MAH, the manufacturer and the other parties set out and agreed who does what for defective medicinal products?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH, the manufacturer and other parties have defined and agreed their respective roles and responsibilities with regard to quality defective medicinal products.

evidence.what: agreed roles and responsibilities between the parties

points.question: For outsourced activities, does the contract set out each party's role for defective products and how to reach the responsible people (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in case of outsourced activities, a contract describes the role and responsibilities of the manufacturer, the marketing authorisation holder and/or sponsor and any other relevant third parties in relation to assessment, decision-making, and dissemination of information and implementation of risk-reducing actions relating to a defective product (recommended). Verify that such contracts also address how to contact those responsible at each party for the management of quality defect and recall issues (recommended).

evidence.what: contracts for outsourced activities

points.question: Do records show timely reporting of quality defects that may lead to a recall or an abnormal supply restriction (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that quality defects are reported in a timely manner by the manufacturer to the marketing authorisation holder/sponsor and all concerned Competent Authorities in cases where the quality defect may result in the recall of the product or in an abnormal restriction in the supply of the product (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect reports sent to the marketing authorisation holder/sponsor and Competent Authorities

points.question: For an investigational product that also has a marketing authorisation, is the authorisation holder told of related quality defects (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in the case of an investigational medicinal product for which a marketing authorisation has been issued, the manufacturer of the investigational medicinal product, in cooperation with the sponsor, informs the marketing authorisation holder of any quality defect that could be related to the authorised medicinal product (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect communications to the marketing authorisation holder

points.question: Does the manufacturer at once tell the competent authority and the MAH when information points to a falsified or suspected falsified product?
points.verify: Verify that the manufacturer informs the competent authority and the MAH immediately of information which indicates that a medicinal product within the scope of its manufacturing authorisation is, or is suspected of being, falsified. Verify that this is done irrespective of whether the medicinal product was distributed within the legal supply chain or by illegal means, including illegal sale via information society services.

evidence.what: procedure for reporting falsified or suspected falsified products
notifications to the competent authority and the MAH

points.question: Does the MAH have a system to take in defect and falsification reports from manufacturers and respond suitably (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH has a system in place to receive quality defect and product falsification reports from manufacturers and that it is able to respond to them in a manner that is appropriate (recommended).

evidence.what: MAH system for receiving quality defect and falsification reports
reports received from manufacturers and the MAH responses

points.question: Does the MAH have systems for dealing with adverse reaction reports?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH has systems in place to deal with adverse reaction reports, as the EU pharmacovigilance legislation obliges it to.

evidence.what: MAH systems for adverse reaction reports

points.question: Does the MAH have robust procedures for managing product recalls (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH has robust procedures for the management of product recalls (recommended).

evidence.what: MAH product recall procedures

points.question: Are the recall arrangements checked from time to time to confirm they still work well (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the effectiveness of the arrangements in place for recalls is periodically evaluated to confirm that they remain robust and fit for use (recommended).

evidence.what: evaluations of recall arrangements

points.question: Do the evaluations of recall arrangements cover office and out-of-office hours, weigh up mock recalls, and are they written down and justified?
points.verify: Verify that the evaluations of recall arrangements extend to both within office-hour situations as well as out-of-office hour situations and that, when performing such evaluations, consideration is given as to whether mock-recall actions should be performed. Verify that such evaluations are documented and justified.

evidence.what: documented evaluations of recall arrangements

points.question: Has the MAH told the Member States concerned straight away about each step to stop or withdraw a product, with the reasons and the stated grounds?
points.verify: Verify that, as obliged by Article 123 of the Directive, the MAH notified the Member States concerned forthwith of any action it took to suspend the marketing of a medicinal product, to withdraw a medicinal product from the market, to request the withdrawal of a marketing authorisation or not to apply for the renewal of a marketing authorisation, together with the reasons for such action. Verify that the MAH also declared if such action is based on any of the grounds set out in Article 116 or Article 117(1).

evidence.what: notifications sent to the Member States concerned
records of the actions taken and their dates

points.question: For veterinary products, does the product database hold the market dates, availability details and any suspension or revocation dates entered by the MAH?
points.verify: Verify that the marketing authorisation holder has recorded in the product database the dates when its authorised veterinary medicinal products are placed on the market, information on the availability for each veterinary medicinal product in each relevant Member State and, as applicable, the dates of any suspension or revocation of the marketing authorisations concerned.

evidence.what: product database entries for the veterinary products

points.question: For veterinary products, has the MAH promptly told the authority about outside bans or limits, new benefit-risk information and any planned stop of marketing?
points.verify: Verify that the marketing authorisation holder informed without delay the competent authority which has granted the marketing authorisation or the Commission, as applicable, of any prohibition or restriction imposed by a competent authority or by an authority of a third country and of any other new information which might influence the assessment of the benefits and risks of the veterinary medicinal product concerned, including from the outcome of the signal management process carried out in accordance with Article 81. Verify that it also informed that authority, or the Commission, as applicable, without delay of any action it intends to take in order to cease the marketing of a veterinary medicinal product prior to taking such action, together with the reasons for such action.

evidence.what: communications sent to the competent authority or the Commission
records of prohibitions, restrictions, new information and intended marketing cessations with dates

points.question: Are returned products that were outside the manufacturer's control labelled as returned and kept apart from clinical use (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that returned products, which have left the control of the manufacturer, are marked as such and segregated so that they are not available for further clinical use, unless without doubt their quality is satisfactory after they have been critically assessed by the person responsible for quality control (recommended).

evidence.what: marking and segregation of returned products
records of returned products and of their critical assessment by the person responsible for quality control

points.question: Is there a system that makes sure every quality complaint, spoken or written, is logged and fully investigated (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that a system is in place to ensure that all quality related complaints, whether received orally or in writing, are recorded and that they are thoroughly investigated (recommended).

evidence.what: complaint handling system description
complaint records and their investigations

points.question: Are the staff who manage complaint and quality defect investigations separate from marketing and sales, or is there a justification (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that personnel responsible for managing complaint and quality defect investigations are independent from marketing and sales departments unless otherwise justified (recommended).

evidence.what: documents showing reporting lines of the investigation personnel
justification where they are not independent

points.question: When the certifying QP is not part of an investigation, do records show the QP was told in good time (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, if the QP involved in the certification of the concerned batch(es) does not participate in the investigation, the QP is informed in a timely manner (recommended).

evidence.what: investigation records showing QP participation or information to the QP with dates

points.question: Do the complaint procedures cover root cause, risk, corrective or preventive measures, recall impact on supply and communications (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that operating procedures have been developed describing the actions to be taken upon the receipt of a complaint, addressing in particular the identification of the potential root cause(s) of the quality defect, the assessment of the risk(s) posed by the quality defect, the need for appropriate corrective or preventive measures, the assessment of the impact that any recall action may have on the availability of the medicinal product to patients, and the internal and external communications to be made (recommended).

evidence.what: operating procedures for complaints

points.question: Where no root cause could be found, do the records name the most likely reasons (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where the root cause cannot be ascertained, the most probable reasons are identified (recommended).

evidence.what: investigation records where the root cause was not ascertained

points.question: When new donor health information affecting quality came in after procurement, was the risk and the need for measures analysed?
points.verify: Verify that, if additional donor (human or animal) health information becomes available after procurement, which affects product quality, an analysis of the risk(s) and of the need for corrective or prevented measures is also made.

evidence.what: records of donor health information received after procurement
analysis of risk(s) and of the need for measures

points.question: When a batch has a known or suspected defect, do records show that the need to check other batches or products was considered (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, when a quality defect is discovered or suspected in a batch, consideration is given to the need of checking other batches (or, as appropriate, other products) in order to determine if they are also affected (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect investigation records

points.question: Do defect investigations look back at earlier defect reports and other relevant information for signs of specific or repeat problems (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that quality defect investigations include a review of previous quality defect reports or any other relevant information for any indication of specific or recurring problems (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect investigation records

points.question: Do investigation records show that risk-management measures for patient safety were put first (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the priority during an investigation is to ensure that appropriate risk-management measures are taken to ensure patients safety (recommended).

evidence.what: investigation records showing the risk-management measures taken

points.question: Is every decision and measure adopted written down (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that all decisions and measures adopted are documented (recommended).

evidence.what: investigation records of decisions and measures

points.question: Is the effectiveness of implemented corrective and/or preventive measures being followed (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the effectiveness of the corrective and/or preventive measures implemented is monitored (recommended).

evidence.what: records of monitoring the effectiveness of the measures

points.question: Are quality defect records kept and used to look for repeat problems (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that quality defect records are retained and used to evaluate the possible existence of recurring problems (recommended).

evidence.what: retained quality defect records
evaluations of recurring problems based on these records

points.question: Were the competent authorities told in good time of confirmed ATMP quality defects that could lead to a recall or a supply restriction (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that competent authorities are informed in a timely manner in case of a confirmed quality defect (faulty manufacture, product deterioration, detection of falsification, non-compliance with the marketing authorisation or Product Specification File, or any other serious quality problems) with an ATMP which may result in the recall of the product or an abnormal restriction in the supply (recommended).

evidence.what: confirmed quality defect records
communications to competent authorities with dates

points.question: Are unplanned deviations left out of the notifications to authorities (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that unplanned deviations as described in Section 11.4 are not notified (recommended).

evidence.what: notifications sent to competent authorities

points.question: Where another entity makes the ATMP, is there a written split of roles for defect assessment, decisions, information and risk-reducing actions (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where the ATMP is manufactured by an entity that is not the marketing authorisation holder/sponsor, the role and responsibilities of the manufacturer, the marketing authorisation holder/sponsor and any other relevant third parties in relation to assessment, decision-making, dissemination of information, and implementation of risk-reducing actions are laid down in writing (recommended).

evidence.what: written roles and responsibilities between the parties

points.question: For blinded trial products, is there a procedure for fast unblinding for a prompt recall that reveals identity no more than necessary (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where the protocol of a clinical trial calls for blinding of investigational medicinal products, the manufacturer has implemented a procedure for the rapid unblinding of blinded products where this is necessary for a prompt recall (recommended). Verify that the manufacturer ensures that the procedure discloses the identity of the blinded product only in so far as it is necessary (recommended).

evidence.what: procedure for rapid unblinding

points.question: Do records show that actions on quality defects matched the risk and put patient protection first (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that measures to address quality defects are proportionate to the risks and that the priority is the protection of patients (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect records showing the risks and the measures taken

points.question: Were planned actions talked through beforehand with the competent authorities concerned, whenever that was possible (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, whenever possible, the actions to be taken are discussed with the concerned competent authorities in advance (recommended).

evidence.what: records of discussions with the concerned competent authorities and their dates

points.question: Is there a written recall procedure covering how to start a recall, whom to inform and how to treat recalled material (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that there are established written procedures for the recall of products, including how a recall is to be initiated, who is to be informed in the event of a recall (including relevant authorities and clinical sites), and how the recalled material is to be treated (recommended).

evidence.what: written recall procedures

points.question: Does the recall procedure provide for matching delivered against recovered quantities and for tracking progress to closure (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the procedure foresees the reconciliation between the delivered and the recovered quantities and the recording of the progress until closure (recommended).

evidence.what: written recall procedure

points.question: Where a defective product is destroyed at the clinical site instead of being returned, is that destruction documented (recommended)?
points.verify: Where destruction of a defective product at the clinical site is used as an alternative to the return of the product, verify that the destruction is documented (recommended).

evidence.what: documentation of destruction at the clinical site

points.question: Are recalled products easy to tell apart and kept separate (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that recalled products are clearly identified and segregated (recommended).

evidence.what: identification and segregation of recalled products

points.question: Can a recall be started quickly at any hour (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that it is ensured that recall operations can be initiated promptly and at any time (recommended).

evidence.what: arrangements for initiating recall operations
staff on how a recall is started at any time

points.question: For authorised ATMPs, has the option of mock recalls been considered as a test of the recall procedure (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in the case of authorised ATMPs, consideration is given to the possibility of performing mock-recall actions in order to test the robustness of the recall procedure (recommended).

evidence.what: procedure or records showing that mock-recall actions were considered

points.question: Were all competent authorities concerned told before a recall began, except in urgent public health cases (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that all concerned competent authorities are informed prior to the initiation of a recall operation unless urgent action is needed to protect public health (recommended).

evidence.what: recall records and communications to competent authorities with dates

points.question: Is there an action plan for product that cannot be recalled because patients have already received it (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that an action plan is established for cases where the product cannot be recalled because it has already been administered to the patient(s) (recommended).

evidence.what: action plan for product already administered

points.question: Has the sponsor agreed the procedures for retrieving investigational ATMPs and recording the retrieval, together with the manufacturer where different (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that procedures for retrieving investigational ATMPs and documenting this retrieval are agreed by the sponsor in collaboration with the manufacturer, where different (recommended).

evidence.what: agreed retrieval procedures

points.question: Do the manufacturer, the investigator and the sponsor's representative know what the retrieval procedure asks of them?
points.verify: Verify that the manufacturer, investigator and the sponsor's representative understand their obligations under the retrieval procedure.

evidence.what: persons concerned on their obligations under the retrieval procedure
records showing the obligations are understood

points.question: Is a detailed list of the manufacturer's shipments kept so that a recall is easier (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, to facilitate recall, a detailed inventory of the shipments made by the manufacturer is maintained (recommended).

evidence.what: inventory of shipments made by the manufacturer

points.question: Do the recall procedures deal with donor health information that arrives after procurement and affects quality (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where donor (human or animal) health information becomes available after procurement, which affects product quality, it is taken into account in recall procedures (recommended).

evidence.what: recall procedures

points.question: Are there written procedures for what to do when a complaint arrives at the manufacturing, storage or importation site (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that there are written procedures describing the actions to be taken upon receipt of a complaint at the manufacturing, storage or importation site (recommended).

evidence.what: written complaint procedures

points.question: Is every complaint written down and assessed for a possible quality defect or other issue (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that all complaints are documented and assessed to establish if they represent a potential quality defect or other issue (recommended).

evidence.what: complaint records and their assessments

points.question: Do the complaint procedures let the sponsor judge whether a complaint warrants a serious breach report (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the procedures ensure that the sponsor is able to assess the complaints to determine if they justify the reporting of a serious breach, as called for by Article 52 of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 (recommended).

evidence.what: written complaint procedures

points.question: Are quality defect investigations carried out following the principles of the referenced EU GMP chapter (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the investigation of quality defect is performed in accordance with the principles detailed in EudraLex, Volume 4, Part I, Chapter 8 (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect investigation records

points.question: Were investigation conclusions discussed promptly between manufacturer and sponsor, with the qualified person and the trial's responsible persons taking part (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the conclusions of the investigation are discussed between the manufacturer and the sponsor, if different, in a timely manner (recommended). Verify that this discussion involves the qualified person and those responsible for the relevant clinical trial in order to assess any potential impact on the trial, product development and on subjects (recommended).

evidence.what: records of the discussion of investigation conclusions, with participants and dates

points.question: Has the sponsor agreed the procedures for retrieving investigational medicinal products and recording the retrieval, together with the manufacturer where different (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that procedures for retrieving investigational medicinal products and documenting this retrieval are, in line with Article 14 of the Delegated Regulation, agreed by the sponsor in cooperation with the manufacturer, where different (recommended).

evidence.what: agreed retrieval procedures

points.question: Do the manufacturer, the investigator and the sponsor's representative know what the retrieval procedure asks of them?
points.verify: Verify that the manufacturer, investigator and the sponsor's representative understand their obligations under the retrieval procedure.

evidence.what: persons concerned on their obligations under the retrieval procedure
records showing the obligations are understood

points.question: Do the retrieval procedures follow the principles of the referenced EU GMP chapter (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the procedures for retrieval of investigational medicinal products are in accordance with the principles detailed in EudraLex, Volume 4, Part I, Chapter 8 (recommended).

evidence.what: procedures for retrieval of investigational medicinal products

points.question: Is a detailed list of the manufacturer's shipments kept so that a recall is easier (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, to facilitate recall, a detailed inventory of the shipments made by the manufacturer is maintained (recommended).

evidence.what: inventory of shipments made by the manufacturer

points.question: Do the contracts between the importing site(s), the third country manufacturer and the MAH or sponsor set out how complaints, defects and recalls are handled (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that adequate provisions are in place between the site(s) performing importation activities, the third country manufacturer and the MAH or sponsor for handling complaints, quality defects and product recalls as set out in Chapter 8 of the EU GMP Guide (recommended). Verify that these provisions are defined in contractual arrangements (recommended).

evidence.what: contractual arrangements between the importing site(s), the third country manufacturer and the MAH or sponsor

points.question: Does the manufacturer have enough qualified people for every task it is responsible for?
points.verify: Verify that there are sufficient qualified personnel to carry out all the tasks for which the manufacturer is responsible.

evidence.what: personnel lists with qualifications against the manufacturer's tasks
staffing of tasks in the plant

points.question: Are each person's responsibilities clearly set, written down and understood by that person?
points.verify: Verify that individual responsibilities are clearly defined and understood by the persons concerned and recorded as written descriptions.

evidence.what: written descriptions of individual responsibilities
persons concerned on their own responsibilities

points.question: Are there enough staff, and do they have the needed qualifications and hands-on experience?
points.verify: Verify that the manufacturer has an adequate number of personnel with the necessary qualifications and practical experience.

evidence.what: personnel records showing numbers, qualifications and practical experience

points.question: Is the load of responsibilities on any single person kept small enough that quality is not put at risk?
points.verify: Verify that the responsibilities placed on any one individual are not so extensive as to present any risk to quality.

evidence.what: written responsibilities of individuals
individuals on the extent of their responsibilities

points.question: Do responsible staff have written descriptions of their specific duties and enough authority to do them?
